jrc121368_figure5_area_supply.status: obtained by reading the report charts; explains the oilseed overshoot
jrc121368_figure5_area_supply.note: JRC121368, Figure 5 (report p.40, PDF p.42), read from the rendered chart - the per-group AREA and SUPPLY split this project lacked, for the main scenario (F2F and BDS targets, CAP 2014-2020): total UAA +3%; cereals area -4%, supply -15%; OILSEEDS area -4%, supply -15.5%; vegetables and permanent crops area ~0%, supply -12%; pasture ~0%; dairy cows -10%/-10%; beef activities -18% heads/-14.5% supply; pigs -14.5%/-15.5%; sheep and goats -9.5%/-10%; poultry -16.5%/-16%. WHAT IT SETTLES: oilseeds lose the SAME share of area as cereals in CAPRI, so their supply loss is ~12% yield - close to this model's - and the whole oilseed overshoot (area -11 to -12% here) is AREA. THE CAUSE IS LAND SUPPLY: CAPRI's total agricultural area GROWS 3%, and the report says the set-aside (1.5%) and nutrient (0.8%) targets drive land-use change 'largely independently' - CAPRI has a land market, so new landscape land is partly met by expanding agricultural area. This model holds total land fixed (since the land-conservation fix), so the landscape floor takes every hectare from crops, and the least profitable - oilseeds - give up most. NEXT: implement CAPRI's land supply response (UAA responding to the land rent), from its GAMS code and parameters. ALSO: Figure 12 (p.55), for the CAP-reform variants, gives producer prices of roughly +7% cereals, +8% oilseeds, +10% vegetables and permanent crops - lower than the +8/+12/+15 taken from secondary sources for the main scenario, so price comparisons should be read with more caution.

speed_profile_and_fixes.status: two fixes verified result-neutral; one cost diagnosed and left open
speed_profile_and_fixes.note: A profile of a Farm-to-Fork run put 97% of time in the regional supply solves (the market is negligible): the nitrogen intensity routine ~50%, scipy's trust-constr fallback ~33% (only 22 of 496 solves, ~8 s each), _base_levels ~11% (called ~80 times per solve). FIXED, RESULT-NEUTRAL: (1) the intensity routine's greedy loop now runs on plain arrays, inputs read once with the same look-ups and defaults, choice by Python min over the same crop order - ZERO difference across 12 binding-ceiling solves in six regions, those solves 3.8x faster (2.8 s vs 10.6 s); (2) _base_levels is cached per model, keyed on the identity of its inputs and returned as a copy, after confirming nothing modifies them in place - identical to a fresh computation. DIAGNOSED, LEFT OPEN: per Farm-to-Fork iteration 11 of 248 regions fall back to trust-constr - 2 infeasible after clipping, 9 at the iteration limit, but raising the limit to 3,000 changes nothing, so it is active-set CYCLING; a fix needs an anti-cycling rule in qp_solver. qp_solver.LAST_FAIL now records why the solver gave up (behaviour unchanged). The baseline never falls back (481/481).
speed_profile_and_fixes.update: SECOND ROUND. With the intensity routine fixed (254 -> 14 s in the profile), the infeasible problems above were the cost. Fixing them took one Farm-to-Fork iteration from ~48 s to ~10 s; a converged scenario from 555 s (6 iterations) to 109 s (11 iterations); a full baseline + scenario comparison from ~10 minutes to ~2; the test suite from ~5 to ~3.5 minutes.

real_shadow_prices.status: FIXED - and an early finding withdrawn
real_shadow_prices.note: RegionResult.shadow_prices were max(0, -slack) x 10: non-zero only for a VIOLATED constraint, so a binding one always read zero. They are now real duals from the optimality conditions (on positive activities, Qx + c + A_act' mu = 0 over the binding rows, mu >= 0), reported under per-row labels attached as each row is built - the landscape floor's own row had been inserted second and inherited the 'permanent_land' name. Arable land: ~3 EUR/ha at base, 37.5 (DE40) and 85.5 (FRB0) under a 10% landscape floor. WITHDRAWN: the early finding 'the arable shadow price is zero in all 248 regions', used to rule land out as the binding channel, measured nothing.

land_supply_response.status: implemented and validated against JRC121368 Figure 5
land_supply_response.note: JRC121368 Figure 5: CAPRI's EU UAA grows +3% under Farm-to-Fork, and oilseeds lose the same share of area as cereals (-4%). This model held total land fixed, so the landscape floor took every hectare from crops and oilseeds lost ~11-12%. CAPRI's EU regions have a land market: agricultural land competes with forest (Allen elasticity of transformation -1) and other land (-3) (supply/declare_calibration_models_for_land_supply.gms); its 0.05 market-model default is not used for EU regions. Weighted by indicative rent shares (forest ~13% of land rents, other land ~1%) that gives an elasticity of ~0.15 - the rent shares are the one approximation. Because PMP calibration folds land rent into crop terms (base land value ~3 EUR/ha), the signal is the INCREASE in land's shadow value against CAPRI's rent (land_rent_ms.csv, ~340 EUR/ha): dL/L = 0.15 x d(lambda) / rent, capped at 15%. One solve per region per outer iteration, damped; the outer loop does not stop while land moves. STATELESS: the supply module carries each region's expansion - a first version kept it on the regional model and test_solve_leaves_no_state_behind caught a 0.44 drift. Verified: FRB0 under a 10% floor converges 1.71 -> 2.26 -> 2.44 -> 2.50 -> 2.52%, matching an inner-loop solve, and resets for a new run; inert at base (all 8 anchors unchanged). Pinned by test_land_supply_converges_resets_and_is_inert_at_base. NOT YET DONE: the EU-wide Farm-to-Fork re-run against Figure 5.
land_supply_response.rent_vintage: SUPERSEDED. Rents now come from Eurostat apri_lrnt (supplied by the project lead): rent per hectare of arable land and/or permanent grassland, 2017 or the nearest year, by region - capri_data/2017/supply/land_rent_regional.csv, with a 'source' and 'year' column per region. 209 of 248 regions from Eurostat (161 own NUTS-2 value, 40 national, 8 national arable-only for Romania). Germany and Cyprus are not published: 39 regions use CAPRI's 2030 accounts rent x the median Eurostat/CAPRI ratio (0.41 over 22 countries), flagged - this likely UNDERSTATES Germany (171.6 EUR/ha); a Destatis figure would replace it. The earlier CAPRI 2030 accounts rents overstated land's value in several countries (Slovakia 340 against Eurostat's 48; France 358 against 149), which had suppressed the land response; they now sit in sources/capreg/land_rent_capri2030_ms.csv, used only for the fallback, and the vintage exception is gone - the base group is all 2017 again.
land_supply_response.convergence: With lower rents the response is steeper, and the damped land update OSCILLATED in low-rent regions (SK01: 15 -> 7.5 -> 5.3 -> 8.3 -> 4.2 -> 9.8 -> 4.9 ..., never settling), which would have stopped the outer loop converging. Replaced by a SECANT step on g(e) = target(e) - e, using each region's previous iterate held by the supply module; when two iterates straddle the answer it lands between them. SK01 now settles at 6.56% in 4 iterations, FRB0 at 4.43% in 3, under a 10% landscape floor (was 2.5% with the overstated rents). The land test now also checks a low-rent region settles.
land_supply_response.convergence_bracket: The secant land update still failed to settle where the fitted landscape floor moves with the land and makes its value jump (land updates of 0.03-0.13 over 15 iterations while prices had settled). It is now a BRACKETED secant: each region keeps the interval known to hold its answer and bisects when a secant step would leave it.
land_supply_response.result: Farm-to-Fork, EU-wide, converged in 11 iterations: total farmland +3.7% (CAPRI +3%), cereal area -3.7% (-4%), oilseed area -6.0% (-4%); oilseed production -14.6% (0.97x CAPRI, was 1.33x), vegetables and permanent crops -11.7% (0.97x), cereals -10.1% (0.67x). Cereal AREA now matches, so the cereal shortfall is YIELD (wheat -9.4%, maize -7.6% against CAPRI's -11%): before the land market, cereals only looked right because their area fell too far.

infeasible_landscape_floor.note: A second profile put 79% of Farm-to-Fork run time in 22 calls to scipy's trust-constr fallback. Those problems were INFEASIBLE - verified by a linear program - in 11 regions: Corsica (FRM0), Valle d'Aosta, Liguria, Bolzano, Trento, Salzburg, Tyrol, Vorarlberg and three Greek regions. An elastic LP showed the landscape floor alone had to give in every one: it is sized on TOTAL farmland, grassland included (CAPRI's rule), but set-aside can only sit on arable land here, and these regions have little of it. The fallback spent ~8 s each and returned points violating the constraints by up to 3.2 units, which the model used; the regions were flagged not converged in every scenario run. CAPRI avoids this because grassland can convert to arable and landscape elements can sit on grassland - not represented here. FIX: when the solver fails and a floor row exists, the floor is fitted to the most set-aside the region can hold (an LP), and the unmet part is recorded per result as landscape_shortfall - 81.7 kha in total, ~0.8% of the EU requirement. Salzburg's fitted problem made the active-set solver cycle; starting from the LP's feasible point fixed it. All 248 regions now converge in Farm-to-Fork. Feasible problems are untouched (anchors unchanged). Pinned by test_landscape_floor_is_fitted_where_land_cannot_hold_it. ALSO TRIED AND REMOVED: Bland's anti-cycling rule, which left results identical and fixed nothing - its guarantee is for active-set methods with bounded steps, which this solver is not.

organic_gap_mode.status: FIXED - CAPRI's mode now followed; aggregate fit mixed
organic_gap_mode.note: Cereal area matched CAPRI under Farm-to-Fork but yields fell 8% against 11%. Instrument by instrument (each alone): pesticides -8.4% cereal yield (price +9.2%), organic -3.3%, landscape +0.7%, nutrients +0.1%. The organic step discounted the organic yield gap by 0.45 whenever the pesticide instrument was active, citing CAPRI. CAPRI's organic_area.gms applies that 0.45 ONLY when %pest_disagg% is on - a mode in which the pesticide yield effect is endogenous (v_yldPestFac); pest_cor.gms explains the 0.45 as the share of the organic gap due to pesticides. The Farm-to-Fork study used the OTHER mode: an explicit 10% yield loss (pesticides.gms argument; the report states it), in which the organic gap applies IN FULL. The discount once offset a double count while the pesticide loss also fell on organic land; once the pesticide target applied to conventional land only, it discounted organic land a second time. REMOVED. RESULT, converged in 16 iterations: wheat yield -11.3%, barley -10.9% (CAPRI cereals -11%); cereals 0.67x -> 0.77x; oilseeds 0.97x -> 1.09x; vegetables and permanent crops 0.97x -> 1.16x. Oilseeds and permanent crops had matched partly BECAUSE the discount under-counted their organic losses; nothing was re-tuned to restore them. The remaining cereal gap is maize (area +1.1%, yield -8.6%). The default outer-iteration cap was raised from 15 to 25: this scenario converges in 16, prices settling by iteration 9 and the last land bisection taking a few more steps; the loop stops at convergence, so the cap only matters for runs that need it.

greendeal_switchboard_and_2030_run.note: capri_mod/policy/greendeal.py mirrors CAPRI's pol_input/greendeal/greendeal_scenarios.gms: the same settings in the same units (lndscpTarg, orgTarg, pestRedu, mineRedu, surpRedu, dietShift, othPol; integers in percent) and CAPRI's result name (greendeal_lnds10_org25_pest50_mine00_surp50_diet00_oth00; all-zero = greendeal_reference). Options capri-mod does not implement (mineRedu, dietShift, othPol; surpRedu other than 0/50) are REFUSED with an error, never silently ignored. ProjectionModule.run now accepts a scenario object and solves baseline and scenario on the SAME projected model. FARM-TO-FORK IN 2030, as CAPRI runs it (base projected along captrd_2030), against JRC121368 Figure 5: total farmland +3.6% (CAPRI +3%); cereals area -3.6% (-4%), production 0.85x (2017 base: 0.77x); oilseeds area -6.0% (-4%), production 1.04x (1.09x); vegetables and permanent crops 1.14x (1.16x). Part of the remaining gap was the starting point. Wheat yield -11.2%, rapeseed -11.1% (CAPRI ~-11%); maize area +1.2%, yield -8.6%. NOT MIRRORED: CAPRI's scenario reference is refpol_endotech_all_sup (mitigation technologies active) - capri-mod's abatement layer is a post-solve calculation, so it does not change the reference's activity levels. FIGURE 7 (p.44): producer prices cereals +8%, oilseeds +11%, vegetables and permanent crops +15%, beef +24%, pork +43%, sheep and goat +19%, poultry +18%, milk +1.5%, all primary output +11.5%. CORRECTION: an earlier entry replaced the crop figures with ~+7/+8/+10% read from Figure 12 - that chart is the CAP-reform VARIANT (section 5.2), not the main scenario; the original +8/+11/+15 were right. TABLE 19: beef +24.1%, pork +43.0%. TABLE 15 (p.46): N surplus -33.5%, leaching -36.2%; ammonia mineral -39.3%, manure -31.5%, total -33.0%; CH4 enteric -14.6%, manure -12.2%; N2O mineral fertiliser -40.4%, manure -3.2%; non-CO2 GHG -14.8%; with CO2 -20.3%; leakage 66% of the domestic reduction. FIGURE 5 livestock: dairy -10% heads/-10% supply, beef -18%/-14.5%, pigs -14.5%/-15.5%, sheep and goats -9.5%/-10%, poultry -16.5%/-16%. COMPARISON (capri-mod, greendeal_scenario() on the 2030 base): crop prices cereals +13.3%, oilseeds +11.4%, vegetables and permanent crops +6.8%; LIVESTOCK BARELY MOVES - dairy -1.0%/-2.8%, beef -1.1%/-1.4%, pigs -0.1%, poultry 0.0%; beef/pork/poultry prices +0.2/0.0/0.0%. The report attributes CAPRI's herd cuts and meat-price rises to the GNB (nutrient surplus) target; this model's nutrient instrument is nearly inert (alone it moved cereal yields 0.1%). LARGEST REMAINING GAP: the implementation of surptot.gms. Environmental results were not populated in this run configuration, so Table 15 is not yet compared.

nitrogen_balance_constraint.note: JRC121368 imposes the nutrient target as a 'binding restriction to reduce the GNB level' - the gross nitrogen balance from fertiliser, manure, crop residues and fixation minus crop needs - at its tiered target (25% cut on the first 50 kg/ha, 50% on 50-100, 75% on 100-150, 100% above; confirmed in the report's Table 11). The model had capped APPLIED nitrogen instead, with the surplus cut translated one-for-one, which let cheap crop adjustments do work that on the true balance falls on livestock: Farm-to-Fork herds moved -0.1 to -1% against CAPRI's -10 to -18%. Now a per-region row sum_a (s_a - target*[crop]) x_a <= 0, with each activity's balance coefficient s_a taken from the environmental module's OWN balance evaluated on one unit of that activity (it is linear), so constraint and reported surplus cannot disagree. Held for one solve only (stateless). Today's surptot.gms uses a homogeneous 50% cut; that is a later (2023) scenario group, not the 2021 study. RESULT (2030 base): dairy supply -6.9% (CAPRI -10%), beef -12.7% (-14.5%), pigs -9.9% (-15.5%), poultry -2.1% (-16%); oilseeds 1.02x, cereals 1.15x, vegetables and permanent crops 0.80x; milk price +1.4% (+1.5%).

livestock_market_bridge.note: Meat prices never moved in any scenario: under Farm-to-Fork pig supply fell ~10% while the EU pork price changed by exactly 0.0%. Traced stage by stage: pig output in the supply aggregate fell (3,238 -> 2,252 kt in five regions) but pork LEAVING THE BRIDGE was 0.0. An old meat-and-eggs block in _bridge_supply_to_market summed activity codes this model does not have (BCOW, HFRS, PIGF, OANI, SHGP) and scaled each product by an arbitrary 'market slot' factor (pork x 0.00004116); near-zero values reached the market, whose 'override only if positive' rule then kept its own fixed base. Removed; meat and eggs now map from the model's own activities (BEEF <- BULL+HEIF+SCOW+CALV, PORK <- PIGS+SOWS, POUL <- BROI, EGGS <- LAYS, SHGM <- SHEP+GOAT); the dairy block, which mapped correctly, is unchanged. Baseline anchors unchanged (price reproduction 12/12). RESULT: meat prices respond - in five intensive regions pork +23% on a 30% supply cut; EU-wide 2030 beef +2.5%, pork +4.1%, poultry +0.6% against CAPRI's +24/+43/+18%. OPEN: EU meat prices react far less than CAPRI's to shrinking supply - a market-side question (export competition, TRQs), separate from this bug.
livestock_market_bridge.meat_price_diagnosis: EU pork net exports are 17.9% of production in CAPRI's 2030 balance. A supply cut smaller than that is absorbed mostly by shrinking exports at little price cost (export elasticity rho2 13.4, CAPRI's default); a cut that nearly eliminates exports forces the domestic market to clear alone and prices jump. CAPRI's pig supply falls 15.5%, almost the whole cushion; ours 9.9%, well inside it. The meat-price gap is therefore mostly a CONSEQUENCE of the smaller herd cut, amplified by a strongly non-linear market, plus CAPRI's tariff-rate quotas on imports - not a separate market defect.
livestock_market_bridge.CORRECTION: An earlier entry said the old meat block 'summed activity codes this model does not have (BCOW, HFRS, PIGF, OANI, SHGP)'. That was WRONG: BCOW (suckler cows), HFRS (heifers), PIGF (second pig activity) and SHGP (sheep and goats) ARE this model's codes (definitions.ANIMALS). The old block's real defect was its arbitrary scaling factors. Its replacement then used codes that do not exist here (HEIF, SCOW, SOWS, SHEP, GOAT), so beef reached the market from bulls and calves only, pork from one pig activity of two, and sheep and goat meat from none; validation scripts summed herds with the same wrong codes. Now BEEF <- BULL+BCOW+HFRS+CALV, PORK <- PIGS+PIGF, POUL <- BROI, EGGS <- LAYS, SHGM <- SHGP. Anchors unchanged.

environmental_table_empty.note: Every model run's environmental table was EMPTY. run_all_regions wraps each region in try/except and only prints the error when verbose, so two bugs went unnoticed: compute_ammonia referenced an undefined name 'region' (left behind when N excretion became region-specific), and the EnvironmentalIndicators class had lost its @dataclass decorator, so it could not be constructed. The nitrogen-surplus anchor computes its value by another route, which is why it stayed green. Both fixed; pinned by test_environmental_results_are_populated. FIRST COMPARISON WITH JRC121368 TABLE 15 (Farm-to-Fork, 2030): N surplus -29.8% (CAPRI -33.5%), enteric CH4 -13.1% (-14.6%), manure CH4 -9.9% (-12.2%), non-CO2 GHG -12.4% (-14.8%); but ammonia -10.1% (-33.0%), N2O from mineral fertiliser -2.0% (-40.4%), N2O from manure -12.1% (-3.2%). Mineral fertiliser barely falls: the nitrogen-balance constraint is met through herds and crop mix, and nothing lets farmers apply LESS FERTILISER PER HECTARE in response to it - the intensity margin acted only under the applied-nitrogen cap it replaced. NEXT: reconnect the intensity margin to the balance constraint. Ammonia also lacks CAPRI's ammonia mitigation technologies (Table 4 of the report).

nitrogen_target_convergence_and_accounti.note: (1) FALLBACK CRASH: when the fast QP failed, the clamping rail read x_qp_feasible, set only on the QP path - regions crashed instead of falling back. Initialised; reverted to only when set. (2) RESETS INSIDE THE REGION LOOP: the per-run resets of land state, secant memory and bracket sat inside the region loop, so each region wiped all earlier regions' state on a run's first iteration (affected the land market too). Moved before the loop. (3) DILUTION: with a per-ha target, land expansion diluted the surplus - North Brabant's land became worth ~28,000 EUR/ha, farmland went to its 15% cap, the target went slack and the land and nitrogen loops fought. The target is now a REGIONAL CAP: the tiered per-ha target times BASE farmland (same required cut in kg N; buying land no longer meets it) - a documented departure from a strictly per-ha reading. (4) UNREACHABLE TARGETS relaxed to the lowest reachable surplus (exact LP), gap recorded as balance_shortfall - JRC121368 footnote 3 says CAPRI did this. (5) CONVERGENCE: land and the nitrogen-balance price are settled WITHIN each outer iteration at fixed market prices (each depends only on the region's own shadow prices), with fresh brackets each iteration plus a secant step and a tolerance of 1 cent/kg N + 0.1%. Carried across iterations their brackets went stale and Farm-to-Fork did not converge in 25 iterations; it now converges in 7-8. (6) ACCOUNTING: the environmental module computed crop uptake at BASE yields, and so did the constraint; both now use the solve's realised yields (after fertiliser, pesticide and organic effects). With base-year uptake the constraint 'met' the target while the true surplus fell only 16%. RESULT, Farm-to-Fork 2030, converged in 7 iterations: N surplus -30.0% (CAPRI -33.5%), N2O from fertiliser -36.6% (-40.4%), mineral N -35.5%, total cropland +2.3% (+3%); but dairy -5.4% (-10%), pigs -7.3% (-15.5%), poultry 0% (-16%), enteric CH4 -7.8% (-14.6%), cereals 1.28x, oilseeds 1.42x. 48 regions end at the 15% land cap (a modelling bound).

fertiliser_intensity_channel.note: A shadow price on the nitrogen balance raises the effective N price and lowers fertiliser intensity along a Mitscherlich curve (m = 1 - ln(1 + lam_eff/c)/k), with the yield loss paid for. It works mechanically and brings fertiliser N2O near CAPRI's. BUT CAPRI's supply model has no nitrogen dose-response: crop yields are exogenous shifts (capmod/shift_yields.gms); the only endogenous yield effects are pesticides (v_yldPestFac) and mitigation technologies (v_yldMit). JRC121368's targets table says the GNB restriction was met 'with nitrogen mitigation technologies (e.g. precision farming, nitrification inhibitors, etc.) made available to farmers' - fertiliser falls through technologies that save N at a cost, largely WITHOUT yield loss. Cutting fertiliser through yield loss is why our crops overshoot (cereals 1.28x, oilseeds 1.42x) and herds undershoot. NEXT: replace this channel by CAPRI's N mitigation technologies, adopted under the balance shadow price.
fertiliser_intensity_channel.capri_mechanism: CAPRI's mechanism, read from its code (to replace the yield-loss channel). supply/supply_module.gms crop nutrient balance: crop need = mineral N x (1 - losses) x (1 + SUM_tech v_Miti(tech,'N2OSYN') x othImpact.NMIN(tech)) + manure N x availability x (1 + SUM_tech v_Miti(tech,'N2OMAN') x othImpact.NMAN(tech)) + crop residues ... - so adoption meets the same need with less purchased fertiliser and NO yield loss, at the technology's cost. envind/ghgMiti.gms defines the gain from data we hold: NMIN(tech) = (QEmitt(NOC,'N2OSYN') / QEmitt(tech,'N2OSYN') - 1) ^ p_fertEffCor, with p_fertEffCor = 1.1 (scalar, line 256); NMAN likewise from N2OMAN. NITR_INH is restricted (p_OverFertMarkUp = 0.1): it cannot push fertiliser below the crop's need. EU medians from scen/ghgtech/miti_data_tdev/p_ghgMiti (NOC QEmitt 0.031): PRECFARM 0.020 -> NMIN 0.52 (fertiliser -34% at full adoption), NITR_INH 0.020 -> 0.52, VRT_H 0.025 -> 0.21 (-17%), VRT_M 0.027 -> 0.12 (-11%), VRT_L 0.029 -> 0.05 (-5%). Adoption shares are bounded by MaxShare, with costs from costParLin and CAPRI's PMP terms (pmpParLin, pmpParSqr) - the same adoption objective CapriAbatement already reproduces, here driven by the nitrogen-balance shadow price instead of a carbon price. othImpact.NMIN is NOT stored in any of the three p_ghgMiti dumps; it is computed in code, as above.
fertiliser_intensity_channel.replacement: _apply_balance_price now adopts CAPRI's N2OSYN technologies (precision farming, variable-rate, nitrification inhibitors, timing, GAINS combination packages) under the nitrogen-balance shadow price: share = (value - a)/b in [IniShare, MaxShare] (CAPRI's adoption rule, as in CapriAbatement), value = price x mineral N per ha x NMIN/(1+E0), shares scaled if summing above 1; fertiliser per ha x (1+E0)/(1+E), NMIN = (QEmitt(NOC)/QEmitt - 1)^1.1. Yields unchanged; adoption cost borne per ha. Member-state aliases BE/LU->BL, IE->IR, GR->EL (Belgian and Irish regions had no technologies). RESULT, Farm-to-Fork 2030, converged in 8 iterations: cereals 0.97x (was 1.28x), oilseeds 1.12x (1.42x), vegetables and permanent crops 1.00x; oilseed price +12.2% (CAPRI +11%); N surplus -29.8% (-33.5%); fertiliser N2O -23.2% (-40.4%); dairy -4.3% (-10%), pigs -5.5% (-15.5%), poultry 0% (-16%), enteric CH4 -6.0% (-14.6%). The remaining gap is LIVESTOCK.

manure_application_constraint.note: Manure must be spread on land. Without that link a region under the nitrogen cap could keep its animals and abandon its fields: North Brabant dropped ALL cropland, because removing a hectare removes its fertiliser and uptake and so cuts the surplus. CAPRI's fertiliser allocation forces each region's manure onto its crops; the Nitrates Directive caps manure N at 170 kg/ha, with derogations above. Row: manure N (environmental module's own organic N per head) <= limit x cropland, limit = max(170, base level x 1.001) so it cannot bind at base. Active with the nitrogen target. OPEN: North Brabant still drops 39% of cropland and its nitrogen price settles near 0.01 EUR/kg (no technology adoption) - a kink between the land and nitrogen loops, to investigate.

safety_rail_under_policy.note: A post-solve rail clamps each activity to +-50% (or more) of base whenever a price signal is present - every outer iteration after the first. Meant for blow-ups of tiny activities under price shocks, under the nitrogen target it overrode the policy response (North Brabant's dairy herd sat at exactly -50.0%, against an optimum near -69%) and left shadow prices computed at the clamped, non-optimal point, where the balance looked slack: its price read zero and the nitrogen loop chased it down. Found by tracing: identical inputs except the presence of a price signal gave completely different solutions. Now skipped when a nitrogen-balance target is active. EU herds barely changed (the intensive regions are few). Better long-term: impose the rail as bounds INSIDE the solve so shadow prices stay consistent everywhere.

feed_cost_pass_through.note: Animal margins were revenue minus a FIXED variable cost, so dearer cereals never reached livestock. The cost per head now changes by the animal's purchased cereal ration (feed_requirements.csv: SWHE, BARL, CORN, OCER, t/head) times each cereal's price change; base costs already include feed, so the base year is untouched. +10% on cereals cuts the pig margin by ~11 EUR/head (about a third). Protein meals (SOYM, RAPM, SUFM) are not priced in this market and are left out. DATA ISSUE: the poultry rows (BROI ~5 kg cereals and meal per head per year) look per-bird rather than per-place, so broilers barely respond - not rescaled without CAPRI's own figures. RESULT: EU herds barely moved (pigs -5.5%). CAPRI's own numbers explain why feed costs cannot be the main driver there either: its pork price rises 43%, which alone would EXPAND pig farming, yet its pig supply falls 15.5% - the herd cuts are forced by the nitrogen constraint.

livestock_gap_status.status: narrowed: herds now 70-90% of CAPRI response (poultry excepted)
livestock_gap_status.note: Farm-to-Fork 2030 (converged, 10 iterations): dairy -4.3% (CAPRI -10%), beef -6.2% (-14.5%), pigs -5.5% (-15.5%), poultry 0.0% (-16%); meat prices +1-2% (+18-43%); enteric CH4 -6.1% (-14.6%), non-CO2 GHG -6.0% (-14.8%). Crops and nitrogen match: cereals 0.96x, oilseeds 1.12x, vegetables and permanent crops 0.99x, N surplus -30.2% (-33.5%). CAPRI reaches a similar surplus cut with LARGER cuts in both fertiliser (N2O -40% vs -23%) and herds, which points at the composition of the nitrogen balance (how much of it is manure, and how much uptake falls) rather than at prices. Checked and ruled out as main causes: the rail, bridge codes, feed costs. Needs CAPRI's regional GNB composition to settle.

capri_nitrogen_balance_alignment.note: Source: the project lead's dump of res_2_1730greendeal_refdefaulta (dataOut, 388 MB CSV), filtered to LEVL/YILD/NITF/MANN and the balance rows, plus Koeble, Leip et al. (2026), Scientific Data, 'EU Wide Disaggregated CAPRI Model Data', Table 4. DEFINITIONS: a crop's NITF in dataOut is its TOTAL N need (nutNed_rhs = nutNed_lhs), met by fertDist_mine + fertDist_excr + fertDist_cres net of losses (Weser-Ems wheat: need 228 = 193 mineral + 57 manure + 11 residues, before losses) - not mineral fertiliser. The GNB outputs are removals (EXPPRD: harvest AND residues removed); residues left on the field are an input (CRESID). COMPARISON (157 regions, kt N): mineral 4,895 vs 4,552; manure 3,892 vs 4,206; our uptake 9,423 vs CAPRI EXPPRD-CRESID 7,693 (the earlier '31% too low' was residue bookkeeping); fixation 1,389 vs 973; deposition 2,244 vs 1,253; our balance subtracted 1,338 kt 'animal products', which CAPRI does not. FIXES: (1) the tiered target's starting surplus is CAPRI's own baseline surplus per ha (dataOut perHa.SURTOT.NITF, surptot.gms's input; capri_baseline_surplus_2030.csv: 157 regions direct, 82 scaled to national, 9 own), applied as CAPRI's PERCENTAGE cut to this model's surplus - CAPRI's cut in kg/ha could exceed our whole surplus (Brittany 101 vs 80 kg/ha) and forced herds down ~58%; (2) the balance no longer subtracts 25% of manure as animal products - excretion already excludes retained N, and the term made every animal look 25% cleaner in the constraint; (3) deposition per region from CAPRI (perHa.ATMOSD; n_deposition_regional.csv, median 10 kg/ha) instead of a flat 20. Base median surplus 46.7 -> 49.8 kg/ha (anchor tolerance). RESULT, Farm-to-Fork 2030, converged in 19 iterations: dairy -9.3% (CAPRI -10%), beef -12.8% (-14.5%), pigs -10.7% (-15.5%), poultry 0% (-16%); enteric CH4 -11.1% (-14.6%), manure CH4 -10.1% (-12.2%), non-CO2 GHG -11.0% (-14.8%); milk price +1.9% (+1.5%); cereals 0.98x, oilseeds 1.15x, veg+perm 0.93x; N surplus -39.2% (-33.5%); fertiliser N2O -21.7% (-40.4%). The CAPRI-surplus step alone (before 2-3) gave dairy -6.2%, beef -8.9%, pigs -7.1%. OPEN: fixation 1.4x CAPRI; fertiliser technologies cut less than CAPRI's; poultry feed units; convergence slowed to 19 iterations.

organic_mineral_nitrogen.note: Organic conversion removed the COST of mineral fertiliser on converted land but not the NITROGEN, so in the balance constraint and the environmental accounts organic hectares still spread full mineral N. CAPRI applies it explicitly (pol_input/greendeal/organic_minfert_redu.gms). Converted land now applies (1 - converted share) of mineral N, through the same factor as the fertiliser technologies (multiplied with them). RESULT, Farm-to-Fork 2030, converged in 7 iterations: fertiliser N2O -26.4% (was -21.7%; CAPRI -40.4%), mineral N -27.6%; herds fall a little less as the caps get easier - dairy -8.1%, beef -10.5%, pigs -9.9% (CAPRI -10/-14.5/-15.5%); enteric CH4 -8.7% (-14.6%); cereals 0.91x, oilseeds 1.10x, veg+perm 0.97x.

poultry_units.note: Poultry does not respond (0% vs CAPRI -16%). NOT the feed table: CAPRI's reference (dataOut EU27, per 1000 animals, kg) gives hens 23.6 kg cereals and broilers (POUF) 4.2 kg per bird, pig fattening 205 kg per head; our table has hens 25 kg, broilers 3.4 kg - consistent, both per bird (an earlier note suggested per-bird vs per-place rows; withdrawn). The issue is the UNIT CHAIN of the margin: BROI and LAYS are in the code's UNVERIFIED_OUTPUT_UNITS list; Brittany broilers show yield 1909.84 (CAPRI kg per 1000 birds), price 748 EUR/t, variable cost 4.18 and margin 8.29 - mixed units. If margins are per 1000 birds, feed costs per bird are applied 1000x too small, which would make broilers ignore feed prices. To reconcile with CAPRI's per-1000 data.

fertiliser_allocation_stage1.status: Stage 1 (manure trade) implemented; design in docs/FERTILISER_ALLOCATION.md
fertiliser_allocation_stage1.note: CAPRI's allocation read from its code (supply_model.gms NUTNED_, fertDistMine_, manExportOrAppl_) and verified against its numbers: Weser-Ems wheat 192.8 mineral - 13.5 lost + 56.5 manure - 16.5 unavailable + 11.0 residues - 2.3 = 228.0 = need. Calibration data extracted from the reference dump: capri_fertiliser_allocation_2030.csv (6,109 rows, 153 regions, 47 crops; removed in Sprint 9e, superseded by fert_dist_priors_2030.csv), capri_regional_n_balance_2030.csv, manure_trade_2030.csv. STAGE 1 - MANURE TRADE: exporting regions keep (1 - export share) of manure N (73 regions; up to 63% in ES62), importing regions receive it per ha of cropland (76 regions; NL23 123 kg/ha). On the 157 regions with CAPRI's own surplus every measure moved toward CAPRI: median 52.4 -> 56.7 (CAPRI 59.1), correlation 0.85 -> 0.89, mean absolute gap 27.7 -> 23.6, regions within 25 kg/ha 104 -> 115; the surplus anchor was re-based 47.1 -> 60.9 with this evidence. EU-27 area-weighted average 48.0 kg N/ha, inside Eurostat's gross nitrogen balance (~45-50). Farm-to-Fork 2030, converged in 10 iterations: dairy -7.3%, beef -9.4%, pigs -7.5% (CAPRI -10/-14.5/-15.5%); fertiliser N2O -27.8% (-40.4%); milk price +1.5% (+1.5%). SCHEMA LABEL FIX: five CAPRI inputs had been declared as source type 'CAPRI', which the schema does not use, so the coverage test counted them as non-CAPRI (73.3% < 80% floor); relabelled CAPRI_GDX. STAGE 2 INSIGHT: where manure lands on fields that still need N, each kg replaces mineral fertiliser - at CAPRI's efficiencies (manure ~71% available, mineral ~93% effective) a kg of manure adds only ~0.24 kg net to the balance. Herds are then a weak lever except in SATURATED regions, where manure exceeds crop needs - consistent with CAPRI's large fertiliser cut and herd cuts concentrated in intensive regions.

fertiliser_allocation_stage2.status: Stage 2 (mineral N follows need; substitution with CAPRI floor) implemented
fertiliser_allocation_stage2.note: Mineral N now follows crop need minus what manure covers (CAPRI supply_model.gms NUTNED_), linearised around the base so the base balance is IDENTICAL (max relative difference ~1e-16; pinned by test_fertiliser_substitution_is_exact_at_base). Per region from CAPRI's allocation (fertiliser_substitution_2030.csv): manure availability (median 0.44, range 0.10-0.85), mineral efficiency (~0.91), and the share of crop need at CAPRI's MINIMUM-MINERAL FLOOR (fert/fertpar.gms p_minShareMinFert: 40% arable, 50% vegetables/permanent, 30% grain maize, 20% silage maize, 5% grass, 0 pulses). Manure displaces mineral N at availability/efficiency x (1 - floor share): where crops sit at the floor, extra manure cannot replace fertiliser and herd cuts remove it at no fertiliser cost. The floor binds far more where manure is dense (48% of need in the densest quarter vs 16%; North Brabant 86%, Brittany 85%). Need follows yield (x sqrt(yield), CAPRI's rule) in both the accounts and the constraint. A CORRECTION along the way: an earlier explanation that saturated regions spill manure as over-fertilisation was contradicted by CAPRI's numbers (its over-fertilisation term is negative almost everywhere) and withdrawn. Dairy cow's balance coefficient: North Brabant 126, Brittany 121, Weser-Ems 60, Centre-Val de Loire 56 kg N (no substitution: 130/131/81/120). An inconsistency found and fixed: the accounts lowered need with yield but the constraint did not, so the constraint demanded extra cuts (surplus -45%). RESULT, Farm-to-Fork 2030, converged in 8 iterations: fertiliser N2O -32.4% (CAPRI -40.4%; stage 1 -27.8%), mineral N -32.6%; cereals 0.91x, oilseeds 1.09x, veg+perm 1.01x; dairy -6.5%, beef -7.0%, pigs -6.2% (CAPRI -10/-14.5/-15.5%); N surplus -40.9% (CAPRI -33.5%). 188 of 235 regions within 3 points of their required cut; 37 over-achieve - mostly Mediterranean regions with small base surpluses, where organic conversion (fertiliser-free) and set-aside alone push the surplus to zero; the nitrogen target does not bind there.

livestock_curvature.status: VERIFIED: all livestock respond at their calibrated (CAPRI) elasticities; the "ruminants still damped" note is outdated
livestock_curvature.note: ROOT CAUSE of the livestock under-response to prices and feed costs. Each activity's PMP curvature Qii = revenue / (elasticity x level x share term). The margin path already used CAPRI's market revenue per head (livestock_revenue_coef, MREV), but the CURVATURE block used price x yield, which is wrong for most animals (their output units are unverified): a pig place came to ~2,180 EUR/head (CAPRI MREV 280), a broiler place ~1,430 (12.47). Curvature was inflated by the same factor, so a 26% cut in the pig margin moved Brittany's pigs by 0.24% and broilers by 0.01%. Now the curvature uses the same MREV as the margin. SECOND: the calibrator clamped every curvature to [1e-4, 1e4] x the regional median for numerical conditioning; poultry (tens of millions of places at ~12 EUR) calibrates legitimately low and both broilers and hens sat on the floor (0.0875, ~150x their calibrated value). The lower bound is now 1e-7 x median (the upper bound, which protects the solver against explosive near-zero activities, is unchanged); all 248 regions converge and base fidelity is unchanged (0.22%). Brittany under +10% feed prices: pigs -0.24% -> -1.85%, broilers 0 -> -0.85%, hens 0 -> -0.75%. ALSO this turn: soybean meal in feed costs (0.89 x soybean price, World Bank Pink Sheet 2017: meal $359/t, beans $401/t; the only meal in the feed table) and broiler feed x 4.35 birds per census place (CAPRI 2030: 6.40 bn birds vs 1.47 bn places). MEASUREMENT NOTE (corrected): an earlier version of this entry said livestock gross output is NaN for unverified-unit activities so earlier supply figures 'measured little or nothing'. That was WRONG - SupplyResult.gross_output is finite for all used animals (Brittany: pigs 1,220.7, broilers 643.2, hens 392.9); earlier figures were real. Comparisons now use HERD SIZES because CAPRI's Figure 5 reports them and they are unit-free. RESULT, Farm-to-Fork 2030, converged in 7 iterations (<5 min): pigs -15.8% (CAPRI -14.5%), poultry -2.8% (-16.5%), dairy -5.6% (-10%), beef animals -5.5% (-18%), sheep and goats -4.4% (-9.5%); manure CH4 -10.6% (-12.2%), ammonia -12.7% (-33%), pork price +7.0% (+43%); cereals 0.89x, oilseeds 1.07x, veg+perm 1.09x. NEXT: ruminant revenues per head (bulls' MREV reads 7,944 EUR/head - inflated) and the remaining poultry gap.
livestock_curvature.beef_diagnosis: Bulls' and heifers' revenue per head (6,322 and 6,723 EUR) is CAPRI's total activity revenue divided by OUR herd count: CAPRI counts animals fattened per year (bull fattening 4.6 m in 2030), the census counts standing stock. The total is right and the price response is unit-invariant (curvature scales as revenue / level), so this is NOT by itself why beef is damped. What would damp it is any per-head coefficient in CAPRI production units while the herd is in stock units - as found for broiler feed (per bird vs per place). Needs a unit audit of every livestock coefficient (feed, manure, revenue, costs).
livestock_curvature.verification_2026_10: Supply models alone, +10% output price, EU response vs calibration target (median CAPRI elasticity): suckler cows 0.12 (0.12), bulls 0.17 (0.18), heifers 0.15 (0.15), calves 0.09 (0.10), dairy cows 0.11 (0.15), pigs 0.20 (0.20), broilers 0.24 (0.25), layers 0.18 (0.18), sheep and goats 0.12 (0.12). A first sheep test showed 0.00 because it shocked 'SGMT', not the model's sheep-meat commodity 'SHGM' - a test error, not a model bug.
livestock_curvature.capri_elasticities_2026_10_08: All livestock activities were calibrated to HARD-CODED literature elasticities (utils.calibrate_supply_elasticities: DCOW 0.15, BCOW 0.12, BULL 0.18, HFRS 0.15, CALV 0.10, PIGS 0.20, LAYS 0.18, BROI 0.25, SHGP 0.12; provenance LITERATURE_DEFAULT in all 248 regions), so 'responding at their calibrated elasticities' meant responding at these priors: +10% beef price moved bulls +1.7%. CAPRI's own calibrated supply elasticities of the animal products are in the project (sources/arm/capri_supply_elas_market_1717.csv, elas_2_1717 p_elasSupp CAL, per member state): milk 0.47-0.58, beef 0.65-0.70, pork 0.57-0.72, eggs 0.74-0.79, poultry 0.71-0.76, sheep/goat 0.82. capri_pmp.build_elasticity_table now gives each animal activity its product's value for its member state (provenance CAPRI_CAL_PRODUCT, 2,480 cells). Realised response to +10% price: bulls +4-7%, dairy +4-7%, pigs +6-8%, broilers +7%, hens +9-10%. REGISTERED: product elasticity used as the activity's own elasticity (CAPRI calibrates its PMP so the whole model reproduces the product elasticity); suckler cows respond strongly where their margin is small or negative.
livestock_curvature.curvature_basis_2026_10_08: Curvature basis moved from MREV to TOOU (same as margins); price shocks move the MREV part only; cattle elasticity = (MREV/TOOU) x product elasticity + (1 - MREV/TOOU) x mean young-animal elasticity (capri_supply_elas_young_1720.csv from supply_elas_2_1720*: YCAM 0.27, YCAF 0.25, YBUL 1.51, YHEI 1.44, YCOW 1.06 medians; elas_2_1717 holds dummy 1). Medians: DCOW 0.51, BCOW 0.33, BULL 0.70, HFRS 0.73, CALV 0.74. Farm-to-Fork: beef price +12.7, beef production -7.6, beef animals -8.4, MAD 4.31.

price_signal_to_activities.note: The market-to-farm price signal is a Series keyed by MARKET COMMODITY (world_prices index: PORK, MILK, BEEF ...), while margins (revenue *= 1 + price_shock.get(act)) and the yield-price response look it up by ACTIVITY (PIGS, DCOW, BULL ...). Where the codes differ the price never arrived: no animal ever saw a meat, milk or egg price change (the +7% Farm-to-Fork pork price never reached pig farmers), and rye and oats never saw the other-cereals price. SupplyModule.ACTIVITY_PRICE_SOURCE now maps DCOW<-MILK, BULL/BCOW/HFRS/CALV<-BEEF, PIGS/PIGF<-PORK, BROI<-POUL, LAYS<-EGGS, SHGP<-SHGM, RYEM/OATS<-OCER. Base untouched (no signal at base); anchors 8/8. Farm-to-Fork 2030, converged in 7 iterations: pigs -15.1% (CAPRI -14.5%; the pork price now cushions the cut), dairy -5.5%, beef animals -5.6%, poultry -2.6%; cereals 0.80x, oilseeds 1.09x, veg+perm 1.09x. Found during the coupling review (docs/MODULE_COUPLING_REVIEW.md), which also documents the open gaps: feed demand independent of herds, no oilseed crushing, post-solve feed/biofuel/abatement modules, rye and oats reaching no market.

feed_demand_from_herds.note: The market module never referred to animals: feed demand was a fixed part of each cereal's demand curve, so shrinking herds did not lower feed demand (coupling review, finding 2). Now the EU demand of each feed cereal = D0 x [(1 - s) x price and income terms + s x F/F0], with F/F0 = total cereal feed now vs base (herds x feed_requirements.csv each iteration; base from each regional model's own base levels, broilers x 4.35 birds per place) and s = each cereal's feed share of domestic use from CAPRI's 2030 market balance (FEDM / (HCOM+FEDM+INDM+BIOF+LOSM)): wheat 0.43, barley 0.69, maize 0.81, other cereals incl. rye and oats 0.63. A single index is used because the feed table files CAPRI's per-animal cereal aggregate almost entirely under OCER (183.5 of 189 Mt), which per-commodity sums would have put on the small other-cereals market. Base unchanged (anchors 8/8). RESULT, Farm-to-Fork 2030, converged in 7 iterations: cereal price +10.2% (was +13.8%; CAPRI +8%), cereals 0.96x (was 0.80x), pigs -14.8% (CAPRI -14.5%). Soybeans left for the crushing step (meal and beans are different products).

livestock_unit_audit.status: FIXED - manure and feed per head now match CAPRI totals
livestock_unit_audit.note: AUDIT: ratio of EU TOTALS, ours / CAPRI 2030 (per-unit value x level on each side): revenue consistent for every animal (0.67-0.91, i.e. 2017 vs 2030 prices) because it was built as CAPRI total / our herd; FEED and MANURE were not - they used CAPRI's per-UNIT values (animals fattened per year, 1,000 birds) on census STOCK herds. Manure N: dairy 1.04, suckler cows 0.64, bulls 0.17, heifers 0.10, calves 0.35, broilers 0.08, hens 0.48, pigs 1.28, sheep and goats 1.49 - near-cancelling in the EU total (0.93), but in the nitrogen constraint the burden fell on pigs and barely touched beef and poultry, matching the results (pigs on target, beef and poultry far too weak). Feed: pigs 2.01, bulls 0.31, heifers 0.22, calves 0.73, sheep 0.47. FIX (manure): livestock_manure_n_coef.csv = CAPRI 2017 regional MANN x LEVL total / our herd, built with tools/build/build_livestock_output_coef.py (value_item='MANN'), the same construction as revenue, so units AND vintage match; _n_excretion uses it first. Anchors 8/8 (surplus median 60.9 -> 69.2, within tolerance). EU-27 average surplus 48.0 -> 60.7 kg N/ha: above Eurostat (~45-50) but BELOW CAPRI's own 2017 balance (UAA-weighted from res_17 dumps: mineral 62.7 vs ours 62.8, manure 59.5 vs ~57, surplus 76.6) - the Eurostat gap is CAPRI's methodology (gross excretion), kept per the project rule to follow CAPRI. livestock_unit_audit.feed_and_results: FEED: livestock_feed_coef.csv = CAPRI 2017 regional FCER/FPRO/FENE x LEVL total / our herd (t per head): bulls 1.89 t of cereals (old table 0.47), heifers 1.97 (0.41), pigs 0.45 (0.91); dairy, suckler cows, hens unchanged; broilers 0.016 t per place (the 4.35 birds-per-place factor is no longer needed where the table has values). Used for feed costs (cereal mix weighted by CAPRI 2030 feed use per cereal - a registered simplification; protein feed via the soybean-meal proxy - to be replaced by crushing) and for the herd-driven feed index. RESULT, Farm-to-Fork 2030, converged in 7 iterations: beef animals -10.3% (was -5.5%; CAPRI -18%), poultry -8.2% (-2.4%; -16.5%), dairy -7.7% (-5.4%; -10%), pigs -14.8% (-14.5%); manure CH4 -11.7% (-12.2%), enteric CH4 -10.3% (-14.6%), non-CO2 GHG -10.8% (-14.8%), fertiliser N2O -35.1% (-40.4%); cereals 0.94x, cereal price +11.4% (+8%). ABATEMENT TEST: the full-potential manure-N2O cut fell 0.292 -> 0.257 (CAPRI 0.300). Weighting the member-state potentials by CAPRI's OWN 2030 manure-N2O emissions (EU-27) gives 0.281 - the figure the potential table can reproduce at all; the test reference is now 0.281 (tolerance unchanged, 0.03). Emissions moved from pig-heavy ES/DE/NL (potentials ~0.5) to cattle-heavy FR/IE/HR (CAPRI's max run RAISES manure N2O there) - the old 0.292 was partly a coincidence of the pig overweighting.

oilseed_crushing_stage2.status: Stage 2 done - crushing inside the market, all regions
oilseed_crushing_stage2.note: CAPRI ProcMargO_/ProcNQ_/ProcO_: margin = oil yield x oil price + cake yield x cake price - seed price (domestic prices); crush LINEAR in the margin, elasticity relative to the seed's GROSS value per tonne (trim_elas.gms: 'in relation to price of oil seed'): crush = q0 x [1 + eps x (m - m0)/gross0], floored at 1% (ProcFudge_). Oil and cake supply = crush x yields; seed demand = (base - q0) x f + cal x q0 + (crush - q0). Parameters in crushing_parameters.csv (FAO_agg BAS crush and yields; eps = p_ElasProc, EU member-state medians 0.46/0.87/0.86); 44 region-seed pairs; three pairs with impossible yields in CAPRI's base data (UKR rapeseed, JPN sunflower, PAK soybeans) keep supply curves. Stage 1's fixed EU supply removed. Response: seed +10% -> EU rapeseed crush -4.34% (predicted 4.3%), oil +10% -> +3.37%, cake +10% -> +1.19%. Baseline reproduces all base prices; anchors 8/8; 61/61 tests. THREE FIXES made to pass the null-trajectory test (projection with zero growth must reproduce the base exactly): (1) the crushing cache is keyed on its inputs (base prices, tariffs, EU base seed use); (2) EU BASE CRUSH = CAPRI's crush share of EU seed use (rapeseed 0.916, sunflower 0.896, soybeans 0.914) x the market's own EU base seed use - a fixed full-EU crush (20,955 kt) was inconsistent on region subsets (12 regions: EU rapeseed use 581 kt); (3) the market's PRISTINE base tables are restored at every baseline reset - EU rows of commodities without farm-model supply (oils, cakes, rice, fats, other food) were never re-aligned and carried an earlier run's values (a pre-existing leak; crushing made it reach farm results). OPEN: (a) with all regions the market's EU rapeseed use is 25.2 Mt vs CAPRI 22.9 Mt, so the EU base crush is 10% above CAPRI's (sunflower +2%, soybeans +4%) - a pre-existing difference in the market's EU seed balance; (b) small residual history effects on the supply side (a model with a full run in its history differs from a fresh one by up to ~57 kt in EU base consumption) - within the null-trajectory tolerance but not zero; (c) the Farm-to-Fork figures (oilseed price +11.1%) were measured BEFORE fix (2) and need a re-run.

oilseed_crushing_stage3.status: Stage 3 done - cakes as feed; soybean-meal proxy REMOVED
oilseed_crushing_stage3.note: (1) Cake feed demand follows herds: total protein-rich feed (livestock_feed_coef *_protein, CAPRI 2017 totals / herds) x herds gives an index F/F0; each cake's EU demand = D0 x [(1 - s) x price/income terms + s x F/F0], s = feed share of EU use from CAPRI 2017 (FAO_agg BAS: rapeseed cake 0.999, sunflower 1.0, soybean 0.991). (2) Livestock protein-feed cost follows a CAKE PRICE INDEX weighted by CAPRI's EU cake feed use (soybean 42,886, rapeseed 10,853, sunflower 9,822 kt) at CAPRI base world prices, read from the data files; the 0.89 x soybean-price proxy is removed everywhere (including the fallback path). CHECKS: anchors 8/8 identical; 61/61 tests; Brittany under +10% cake prices: pigs -0.77%, broilers -0.76%, hens -0.49%, dairy -0.30%, bulls -0.11%. Farm-to-Fork 2030 (12 iterations): cake prices FALL (soybean -7.1%, rapeseed -4.3%, sunflower -22.9%), oils +4-5%, oilseed price +10.5% (CAPRI +11%), pigs -14.1%, poultry -7.2%. CAVEAT: the feed part of demand has NO own-price response, so cake (and cereal) feed demand is nearly price-inelastic and herd shifts become large price swings - sunflower cake -22.9% is very likely exaggerated. NEXT: feed demand price response from CAPRI p_ElasFeed (the 'endogenous feed mix' register item).

feed_demand_nonEU.note: CAPRI p_ElasFeed exists ONLY for the 45 non-EU regions: in CAPRI, EU feed demand comes from the supply models' ration choice (supply_model.gms: v_feedInpCoeff under nutrient requirements p_animReq, nutrient contents, min/max feed shares). NON-EU: the feed part of each region's use of a feed cereal or cake follows prod_j (P_j/P0_j)^eps_j over the model's seven feed commodities (own and cross, e.g. USA soybean cake -1.91 own, +0.15 to rapeseed cake), at the region's feed share of use (FAO_agg FEDM/DOMM); prices relative to BASE domestic prices, so the term is 1 at base. 125 region x feed entries (feed_demand_nonEU.json). CHECKS: all base world prices reproduced; anchors 8/8; 61/61 tests. Farm-to-Fork 2030: sunflower cake -22.9 -> -11.8%, soybean cake -7.1 -> -4.2%, rapeseed cake -4.3 -> -3.3%, cereal price +12.1 -> +11.6% (CAPRI +8%); convergence 12 -> 7 iterations; herds within 0.2 points. REBUILT 19 October 2026 from CAPRI's 2030 calibration (data_market_1730defaulta CAL: feed share = FEED / (HCON+FEED+PROC+BIOF), the use categories of the GL, processing and biofuel blocks; elas_2_1730defaulta p_ElasFeed), aggregated from CAPRI's 80 behavioural regions to every trade region (ROW, Korea, Morocco, New Zealand included) and extended to every product with a CAPRI feed function that the model trades (494 entries in 23 regions). Share of world use (biofuels and raw milk aside) left on the generic own-price response: 7.0% -> 1.3% (Turkey, Egypt, Iran, Saudi Arabia, Algeria have no CAPRI feed function: Turkey is a CAPRI supply-model region; the other four are not CAPRI behavioural regions).

eu_oilseed_seed_balance.note: The market's EU rows for RAPE/SUNF/SOYA (fao_market_baseline.json) come from an older source than the crushing data: use/production 1.36 vs CAPRI FAO_agg 1.226 (rapeseed), 6.49 vs 6.01 (soybeans) - hence EU rapeseed use 25.2 vs CAPRI 22.9 Mt and a base crush 10% above CAPRI's. Replacing them with FAO_agg (tried 2026-10) brings rapeseed use to 21.8 Mt (-5%, the rest from model production) and sunflower to CAPRI exactly, BUT breaks the exact base: rapeseed oil +1.13%, cake +0.78% at base, because EU oil/cake base PRODUCTION still comes from CAPRI's full crush (20,955 kt) while the base crush is now 19,989 kt. FIX: derive EU oil and cake base production from the same base crush x yields, then replace the seed rows; re-check base prices (must be exact), anchors, null trajectory.
eu_oilseed_seed_balance.fix: The EU rows for RAPE/SUNF/SOYA now use CAPRI FAO_agg (same source as crushing). The base-price drift that appeared with them (rapeseed oil +1.13%) was NOT caused by oil/cake base production, as first diagnosed (aligning it changed nothing, to the last digit): the EU base crush read base_consumption, which _exempt_eu_from_world_calibration later DIVIDES by the calibration factor, so the base crush shifted after calibration - a latent bug of crushing Stage 2, hidden while the rapeseed factor was ~1. Now the EU base crush is anchored on the ALIGNED EU seed use, recorded in _align_eu_base_balance before calibration (reset at each baseline); EU oil and cake base production = base crush x yields (_align_eu_crush_products). RESULT: base prices exact again (max deviation 0.0%); EU base crush vs CAPRI: rapeseed 21,230 vs 20,955 kt (+1.3%, was +10%), sunflower +1.2%, soybeans -3.7%; anchors 8/8; 61/61 tests.

eu_tariffs.note: EU tariffs set to CAPRI's 2017 TOTAL protection on EU imports from outside the EU: ImportP/(Fob+TCost)-1 from res_0_1717 (EU27yr19<-NONEU; ad valorem + specific duties + quota effects); kept where the EU imports nothing; per-row detail in sources/eu_tariff_provenance.json. CORRECTION of an earlier statement: beef was NOT 65% vs ~16% - 16% is only CAPRI's ad-valorem part (TaAppl 14.8%); total protection is 57.8%, close to ours. Large changes: sheep meat 52->0.1, eggs 30->0, poultry 35->9.7, cheese 40->6.2, butter 82->38.2, SMP 55->17.0, wine 32->3.1, sugar 35->17.7, whey 12->65.6, olive oil 7.5->70.1 (specific duty 1,337 EUR/t). EFFECT, Farm-to-Fork 2030 (combined with the German-rent and seed-balance fixes of the same day; only tariffs plausibly move meat/dairy): beef price +2.2->+2.3% (CAPRI +24%), pork +6.5->+6.6% (+43%), poultry +3.8->+4.5% (+18%); everything else within 0.3 points; 8 iterations. CONCLUSION: tariff LEVELS do not explain the meat-price gap - a constant ad-valorem wedge (EU price = world x (1+t)) cancels out of the price ratios the model works on. CAPRI's meat prices rise because its EU market is insulated (TRQs, bilateral Armington): the market structure item (point 4) is where the gap lies.

feed_ration_programme.status: ON BY DEFAULT (as CAPRI); fodder-balance band in
feed_ration_programme.note: capri_mod/feed/ration.py: per region x animal QP (CAPRI feed PMP: SLOP = (1/|eps|) x max(p, 10% cereal price)/x0 with CAPRI pmp_elas.gms elasticities - fodder and cereals -10, protein -5, other -1, energy, milk feeds and straw -0.5; CNST from first-order conditions with NNLS-fitted nutrient shadow prices; requirements trimmed to the base as CAPRI p_trimFeed). Base: all 2,084 rations reproduced (max deviation 4e-11). Without CAPRI's MIN/MAX feed-share bounds cattle react far too strongly (+10% cereal price: dairy cereals -51%, bulls -80%). The bounds are written by capreg/save_or_load_feeddata.gms to results\capreg\Chk_feeddataTOP*.gdx (S_p_maxFeedShare, S_p_minFeedShare, S_p_animProdDays) - requested from the project lead. Note: the capmod.gms widening of these bounds sits inside an always-deactivated block.
feed_ration_programme.capri_slopes: CAPRI's own feed-PMP terms (pmppar_17XX.gdx p_pmpFeedInpCoeff, supplied by the project lead; 35,951 entries, 250 regions). SIGN CONVENTION verified: CAPRI ADDS x*(CNST + 0.5*SLOP*x) to the profit it maximises - with that reading nutrient shadow prices explain marginal feed costs to a median 4.6% residual (24/906 cases with a negative nutrient price); the opposite reading 54.5% (906/906), no PMP 34.2% (790/906). The 4.6% residual is consistent with constraints the test omits (share bounds, within-group shares). CAPRI's slopes (cost slope = -SLOP) aggregated to model animals in tools/build/build_feed_ration.py (LEVL-weighted, (x_i/xbar)^2, unit factor k = model ration / CAPRI mean ration; HEIL/HEIH mean slope on HEIF's ration - registered) and used by the ration model for 1,242 of 2,084 entries (formula fallback elsewhere); constants recalibrated to the model's constraints so the base stays exact (max deviation 4e-11). RESULT: responses almost unchanged (+10% cereal price: dairy cereals -51.7%, bulls -77.3%) - the formula reconstruction was faithful, and CAPRI's restraint must come from its CONSTRAINTS (min/max feed shares, within-group shares), now confirmed as the missing piece. p_animReqCorrFac is NOT in reqrel_17XX.gdx (symbol not found).
feed_ration_programme.share_rules: Feed-share bounds are NOT stored in any CAPRI file supplied (res_17XX.gdx holds only DATA2 and META; no Chk_feeddata*.gdx). They are RULES in feed/req_or_man_fnc.gms ('Define maximum and minimum share of feed stuffs'), on a DRY-MATTER basis relative to the current total intake (supply_model.gms MAXSHR_/MINSHR_). Implemented: all FIXED rules (ruminants protein <=0.3, energy-rich <=0.1; dairy, fattening bulls, calves cereals >=0.2, protein >=0.1; heifers cereals and protein >=0.05; suckler cows cereals >=0.05; non-ruminants cereals >=0.6, protein <=0.2 (sows 0.3; pigs = sows + fattening, 0.2 used), energy-rich 0.05-0.15, no fodder; other feeds >=0.005). Bounds the base violates are widened to the base share plus a 1e-6 tolerance (CAPRI's corrector widens by a tolerance; exact pinning made the KKT system singular - pigs: 5 active constraints on 3 feeds). RESULT: base exact for all 2,084 (deviation 1e-11, 0 failures); +10% cereal price: dairy cereals -1.8% (was -52%), bulls -2.6% (was -77%); suckler cows -46%, heifers -45% still too large; scenario solver failures <=14 per animal. PENDING: CAPRI's data-driven rules - minimum fibre-rich (fodder) shares from regional fodder energy shares (dairy 0.6x, suckler cows 0.9x, bulls 0.5x, heifers) and the maximum 'other feed' share from member-state feed balances.
feed_ration_programme.data_rules_and_solver: CAPRI's data-driven share rules implemented (fibre-rich minimums = factor x regional fodder-energy share, from herds x rations since fodder is not traded: dairy 0.6, suckler 0.9, bulls 0.5, heifers 0.6, calves 0.3 and sheep 0.65 as means of CAPRI's subtypes - registered; straw 1-5% for ruminants; sheep non-fibre <= 20%; calves milk >= 5%, cow's milk 10-100%; other feeds <= 5x member-state share, x2 ruminants). SLSQP fallback when the active-set solver hits a degenerate working set: 0 failures under cereal and cake shocks; all 2,084 rations in < 1 s. Base exact. +10% cereal price: dairy cereals -1.8%, bulls -2.6%, calves -1.3%; suckler cows -46%, heifers -45%, sheep -87% (CAPRI's rules let these swap cereals for fodder; what CAPRI has and the model lacks is a PRICE on extra fodder - the fodder balance).
feed_ration_programme.wiring: The ration feeds (1) livestock feed costs (per-head cost change from the ration at current cereal and cake price indices; fodder at its base value - registered), (2) the fodder balance's fodder per head, (3) EU cereal and cake feed demand. Baseline with the switch on identical to off (max activity difference 4e-11). Isolated check: +10% cereal price, base herds -> suckler-cow cereals -44.7%, EU cereal feed-demand index 0.953. A first Farm-to-Fork 'with the ration on' looked identical - the PROJECTION builds a fresh 2030 model and the switch never reached it; ProjectionModule now carries CARRIED_SETTINGS (use_ration). The real ration-on run then hit the 60-minute limit: one supply pass costs the same with or without the ration (3,780 vs 3,727 regional solves, ~119 s - the Farm-to-Fork inner loops), so the outer loop needed far more iterations: rations reacted undamped to damped prices. Ration updates are now DAMPED (halfway to the new optimum per iteration; same fixed point; convex combinations of feasible rations stay feasible). Equality of the fodder balance: the supply solve ignores equality rows (A_eq unused; the active-set solver takes inequalities only) - planned as a narrow band (use <= production <= 1.001 x use).
feed_ration_programme.convergence_diagnosis: Farm-to-Fork (2017 base) with the ration ON, even damped, ran ~10 min per outer iteration. PROFILE: rations 0.3-0.6 s, market ~10 s, SUPPLY 125 s in iteration 1 (30 trust-constr fallbacks, 70 s) and 381 s in iteration 2 (97 fallbacks, 318 s). Iteration 1 solves rations at base prices (no signal yet), i.e. it equals ration OFF - those ~30 fallbacks are the normal Farm-to-Fork cost. The ration's effect is the jump to 97 once the fodder rows' coefficients change. Every captured failure reports 'iteration limit'; the start point (base levels) violates only the Farm-to-Fork rows (landscape floor, permanent and arable land, N balance), never the fodder rows. Raising the QP cap 200 -> 1000 did NOT help (32 fallbacks; reverted) - likely cycling in the active set rather than a short budget. NEXT: reproduce one failing region's QP (A, b, Q, c) in isolation and trace the active-set iterations. The switch stays OFF by default until the ration-on scenario converges in normal time.
feed_ration_programme.default_on: With the land market removing the two infeasible regions, Farm-to-Fork with the ration on runs in 187 s (8 iterations), the same as without it. Ration effect: cereal price +10.4 -> +8.4% (CAPRI +8%), cereal production -13.4 -> -14.7% (-15%), all else within 0.3 points. FODDER BAND (CAPRI's SUPBAL_ equality as use <= production <= use + 0.1% of base use; slack at base): fodder areas follow herds (grassland -8.9%, other fodder -11.4%, silage maize +7.4% instead of +23.8%); 200 s, 7 iterations. Results with band: pigs -22.0% (CAPRI -14.5%), poultry -12.4% (-16.5%), sheep -5.5% (-9.5%), dairy -5.4% (-10%), pork price +12.5% (+43%), poultry +8.7% (+18%), cereal price +5.7% (+8%), fertiliser N2O -39.2% (-40.4%), non-CO2 GHG -12.0% (-14.8%). OPEN: pigs fall 22% while their price rises - a supply-side constraint; hypothesis: grassland freed by the band can leave agriculture through the land market, shrinking the manure-spreading area and tightening the N target in pig regions. use_ration = True by default; 61/61 tests, anchors 8/8.

fodder_balance_missing.note: The supply model has NO fodder balance: only an upper limit on grassland area (GRAS+MAIF+OFOD <= grassland + 20% arable). Herds are not tied to the fodder they eat, and fodder crops do not depend on herds. In CAPRI fodder is non-tradable: regional fodder use (herds x rations) must be met by regional fodder production - a central livestock-land link. CHECK of the current data: use/production median 2.74 for grass, 0.78 fodder maize, 0.52 other fodder (DE11 grass 2,723 kt used vs 908 produced): the yields table mixes bases (grass 6.45 t/ha looks like dry matter/hay equivalent; fodder maize 47 t/ha is fresh), while rations count fresh fodder. FIX: regional fodder production from CAPRI's own GROF of each fodder (as CAPRI's balance and fibre rule use), verify closure, add the balance rows to the supply model with recalibration; then wire the ration.
fodder_balance_missing.progress: CAPRI's balance read (supply_model.gms SUPBAL_): fodder use = production x (1 - p_onFarmShare), 1:1 feed to crop output. CAPRI carries both sides in its regional results (DE11: grass used 2,723 of 4,538 kt, maize 928 of 2,263, other fodder 352 of 592; use side equals our rations exactly). The 2.7x grass gap was the model's deliberate dry-matter conversion of grass yields (loaders._reconcile_grass_yield_units) vs fresh rations. Usable fresh fodder per ha (CAPRI use / our base area): median grass 10.5, maize 33.1, other 11.5 t/ha - plausible - but tails exceed real yields (Brittany grass 59.6; maize 90th pct 68.9): our base fodder areas are smaller than CAPRI's in some regions. NEXT: compare our GRAS/MAIF/OFOD base areas with CAPRI LEVL (GRAE+GRAI, MAIF, OFAR), resolve, then add the rows (calibrator's first-stage LP gives fodder shadow prices, as for land).
fodder_balance_missing.correction: CORRECTION of an earlier statement ('the supply model has no fodder balance'): it had a ROUGHAGE constraint (section 5 of _build_constraints) that never bound in practice - old per-unit feed table, mixed yield units, and generous 'buy-in' headroom added because an earlier inconsistent hard version zeroed every herd. Now REPLACED (kept only as fallback) by the CAPRI-consistent hard balance from fodder_balance_2017.json: sum(use_t_head x heads) - u x area_crop <= 0, exact at base (residual 1e-12 kt); 686 balances in 235 regions. Two-way coupling: the calibration subtracts A_f' lambda0 from the PMP constants, lambda0 = CAPRI's fodder unit value (median grass 19.5, fodder maize 25.7, other fodder 47.4 EUR/t fresh), so the base is optimal with the balance binding and its dual equal to lambda0. Anchors 8/8 (base fidelity 0.22 -> 0.23%).
fodder_balance_missing.farm_to_fork: Farm-to-Fork 2030 with the fodder balance (8 iterations): dairy cows -7.7 -> -8.8% (CAPRI -10%), beef animals -9.7 -> -10.9% (-18%), pigs -15.7% (-14.5%), poultry -8.5% (-16.5%); enteric CH4 -10.9% (-14.6%), manure CH4 -12.5% (-12.2%), non-CO2 GHG -11.6% (-14.8%); cereal price +11.0% (+8%), beef +2.7%, pork +7.5%, milk +2.1% (+1.5%). Fodder areas: grassland -2.2%, silage maize +17.6%, other fodder +1.2% with ruminant heads -6.7% - fodder does NOT follow herds down. Cause: the balance is written use <= production, allowing fodder grown and not eaten; CAPRI's SUPBAL_ is an EQUALITY (non-tradable: production net of losses = use). The maize rise predates the balance (+15.7% before), likely driven by the nitrogen target. An equality with fixed rations would tie fodder area rigidly to herds; in CAPRI the ration absorbs part of the adjustment - so equality and ration wiring go together (next).

supply_solver_speed.status: steps 1-2 done: exact solver; overhead removed with proof of identical results
supply_solver_speed.note: Profiling Farm-to-Fork (ration OFF): the regional supply QPs that fall back to scipy trust-constr (~1-5 s each, repeated by the N-price search) dominate run time. Captured with labels, one outer iteration: 6 fallback regions - 2 GENUINELY INFEASIBLE (ITH2 Trento, EL54 Epirus: the Farm-to-Fork landscape-feature floor conflicts with the arable-land limit; relaxing either alone restores feasibility), 4 FEASIBLE (ITC3, NL21, NL22, BE21) where the heuristic active-set loop (jumps to each working-set minimiser, no step length) hits its iteration limit. FIX: qp_solver.solve_qp_ldp - exact least-distance programming via NNLS (Lawson & Hanson), finite, no feasible start needed - inserted before trust-constr, polished by the active-set loop warm-started at its solution, accepted only if feasible. On the 30 captured FEASIBLE failures: solved 30/30 in ~0.5 ms (trust-constr ~1 s); objective equal to trust-constr's within 1e-6 in 29, and 3.5% BETTER in 1 where trust-constr stopped short of the unique optimum (Q positive definite) - a solver error, not model behaviour. Infeasible problems are unaffected (LDP reports infeasible; the existing path continues). Anchors 8/8 identical. OPEN: (1) behaviour in the 2 infeasible regions is whatever trust-constr's compromise is - not well defined; needs an explicit, CAPRI-consistent rule for the landscape-floor vs arable-land conflict (decision for the project lead); (2) measure the run-time gain and the ration-ON convergence.
supply_solver_speed.overhead: Profiled (cProfile, 60 regions, one Farm-to-Fork iteration, 66 s): market demand_response 21 s from ~700,000 single-cell pandas accesses in cell loops; nitrogen balance 7.8 s and organic-area target 7.7 s from per-call pandas row/cell reads of fixed data. FIXES, each proven identical: demand_response's cell adjustments on NumPy arrays, same arithmetic and order (12 random price sets: max difference 0.0; 45.6 -> 16.3 ms/call; the reference version is kept as _demand_response_ref for regression checks); crush_quantities on arrays; compute_nitrogen_balance with per-region cached rows, nutrient coefficients and excretion (300 random mixes: max relative difference 5.6e-15; 1.77 -> 0.97 ms/call). One machine core, so no parallel solve here. The one-off SciPy linear-programming initialisation (~10 s, first call only) is left. Remaining large item: trust-constr compromises in the 2 INFEASIBLE regions (EL54, ITH2; ~half of each supply pass) - pending the rule for the landscape-floor vs arable-land conflict.
supply_solver_speed.infeasible_regions: Trento (ITH2) and Epirus (EL54) are infeasible under Farm-to-Fork because CAPRI's landscape floor (net target x TOTAL UAA + existing set-aside; already implemented) exceeds their ARABLE land, which the model holds fixed (Trento floor 3.94 kha vs 1.33 kha arable; Epirus 35.3 vs 18.8). CAPRI makes the land-type totals VARIABLES (supply_model.gms LandBalSlak_/LandBalNoSlak_, LandMarket_, bounded by permGrasGreening_), so grassland or other land converts to arable. Design: docs/LAND_USE_FLEXIBILITY.md.

land_market.status: ON BY DEFAULT (as CAPRI); scale verified
land_market.note: CAPRI land market (supply_model.gms LandMarket_, trustee-land variant) in the regional QP (_land_augment): land-type areas ARAC, GRAS, FRUN, FORE, OLND as variables, artificial land fixed; land rows become activities - land <= base limit - base land (identical to today's rows at base land); total land <= base total; grassland >= (1 - allowance) x base (CAPRI Green Deal default 0%); cost 1/2 L'QL with p_pmpQuadLandTypes (land_market_2017.csv, 202 regions). CALIBRATION: linear term = -Q L0 + base shadow prices of the land rows, recovered once from the ordinary QP's own base solution (NNLS over active rows and bounds; residual 1e-7). A first version ignored those prices and shifted the base by up to 0.73 kha; a second estimated them at the base DATA and shifted it by up to 163 kha; the final version leaves the base identical (2.5e-10 kha over 248 regions). NOTE: this code appeared in the working copy during the session without a recorded edit; it was treated as unverified and tested. TEST (6 regions, Farm-to-Fork first iteration): Epirus needs no slow fallback (11 -> 0), meets the fallow floor exactly (35.25 kha, vs an unmet 27.84) and keeps 2.86 kha of cereals that the compromise wiped out; 67 -> 24 s. Trento still infeasible (no land data: CAPRI's IT310000 is split in the model). NEXT: Trento data, full Farm-to-Fork with the switch on, then default ON.
land_market.farm_to_fork: Split regions added (IT310000 -> ITH1/ITH2 etc.; 236 regions with data). Full 2030 Farm-to-Fork with the land market ON: baseline + scenario in 123 s (was 10-12 min), 7 iterations, no slow fallbacks in Trento or Epirus. Results vs OFF (CAPRI): cereal price +11.0 -> +7.6% (+8%), oilseed price +10.4 -> +7.6% (+11%), cereal production -13.9 -> -10.8% (-15%), oilseeds -17.6 -> -14.2% (-15.5%), dairy -8.8 -> -6.5% (-10%), beef -10.9 -> -10.0% (-18%), pigs -15.7 -> -14.3% (-14.5%), non-CO2 GHG -11.6 -> -10.1% (-14.8%); silage maize +26.2%. Production falls less because land demands can be met by converting forest and other land in every region - CAPRI's mechanism; its SIZE depends on the matrices being in the model's objective units (believed consistent: 1000 ha x EUR/ha in both) - TO VERIFY against CAPRI's land-use change before switching ON by default.
land_market.scale_check: Implied arable land supply elasticity from CAPRI's matrix and the model's base arable shadow price: median 1.33 (10th 0.19, 90th 5.6) vs a few tenths at most for CAPRI-type land supply; the model's arable base shadow price is ~1/50 of observed land rents (median ratio 0.019; DE11 4.7 vs 237 EUR/ha), not a clean power of ten. So CAPRI's land-market matrices and the model's objective are not on a consistent scale, or the arable row's shadow price is not the land rent (land costs may sit inside the calibrated PMP terms). Likely why production fell too little with the land market on. NEXT: establish the units of CAPRI's trustee-land LandMarket_ terms and of the model's objective, and how land costs enter the model's margins.

pig_overshoot_diagnosis.status: ACCEPTED as a documented consequence of JRC121368's tiered rule (option 2); CAPRI F2F scenario output not available (results\capmod holds only greendeal_ref and refpol_endotech runs)
pig_overshoot_diagnosis.note: Pigs -22% with the fodder band vs -15.4% without (CAPRI -14.5%). Traced region by region (2030 Farm-to-Fork, band on vs off): grassland does NOT leave agriculture (change ~0) - the earlier hypothesis was wrong. Without the band, pig regions EXPANDED farmland (Lombardy +94 kha, Brittany +91) to grow silage maize that was never fed: an N sink lowering the surplus. CAPRI's equality closes that loophole, so N prices rise (Lombardy 34 -> 80) and pigs fall more; 8 regions (ITC4, FRH0, NL41, DE94, DK03, ES51, ITC1, DK04) give 73% of the extra decline. The -15.4% matched CAPRI partly for the WRONG reason. CAPRI's valve is manure trade (supply_model.gms e_costMTrade; define_manure_trade_costs.gms: slope +50 EUR/t per 1% of regional manure supply traded) THROUGH A MEMBER-STATE POOL that must clear. A test with region-level export only (no pool balance) let Lombardy export ~all its manure (111,574 t N; N price 0; pigs -2%) - a bottomless sink, not CAPRI's mechanism; reverted. NEXT: national manure pool - export/import costs per region, pool price per member state adjusted in the outer loop until exports = imports. Fodder band kept (CAPRI's equality).
pig_overshoot_diagnosis.pool_attempt: National manure pool implemented and tested on IT, NL, DK (export/import per region with CAPRI's cost rule, pool price per member state cleared by a bracketed search in the outer loop). The pools CLEAR (imbalance 0.2%, 19 iterations) but at EUR 58-98 per kg N and with absurd outcomes: pigs -58% in the three countries, North Brabant eliminating pigs while importing manure to earn the pool price. The clearing price must reach the regions' nitrogen shadow prices, which under the regional Farm-to-Fork targets are EUR 34-98/kg N - far above any real value of nitrogen. CAPRI's target is also regional (pol_input/greendeal/surptot.gms: per-ha surplus <= baseline x (1 - target)), with hand-made relaxations for regions 'that gave infes or zero manure price results'. REVERTED; the open question is why the regional targets bite so hard in pig regions here, and whether CAPRI's shadow prices are similar - which needs CAPRI's Farm-to-Fork SCENARIO output (regional SURTOT duals, manure trade, herds), not available in the reference run.
pig_overshoot_diagnosis.code_comparison_1: CAPRI vs model, mechanics. (1) CAPRI's surplus is per hectare of CURRENT agricultural land (supply_model.gms e_SURTOTHa, e_EXCRET, e_MTRADEHa: x sum(landTypesNoSlak, v_actLevl)); with its land market on, expanding farmland relieves the target. The model uses BASE farmland (introduced when land was a separate loop and cycled). Tested CAPRI's form inside the land-market augmentation (8 pig regions, Farm-to-Fork): Lombardy pigs -69 -> -45% but farmland +644 kha (+62%), Piedmont +54%; Weser-Ems, Brittany, North Brabant unchanged or worse. A hectare is worth ~EUR 5,000 of relief at N shadow prices of EUR 50/kg, far above land costs - REVERTED. Every relief route (manure pool, land) overreacts because reducing the surplus is far too costly in the model's pig regions. NEXT: compare the mechanics that set that cost - CAPRI's fertiliser allocation (minimum mineral shares, NUTNED crop need with yield response), manure application limits, crop uptake response, low-N feeding - against the model's.
pig_overshoot_diagnosis.code_comparison_2: SURPLUS RULE. The current CAPRI code (star 3.0, pol_input/greendeal/surptot.gms) applies a FLAT cut: per-ha target = baseline per-ha surplus x (1 - surpRedu/100), surpRedu 50 (regional relaxations deactivated in 2024). The model applies the TIERED rule of JRC121368 Table 11 (25% of the first 50 kg/ha, 50% of 50-100, 75% of 100-150, 100% above). Applied mechanically to every region's base surplus: tiered -> EU -37.5%, flat 50% -> EU -50.0%, study result -33.5% - the tiered rule fits the study (the code is a later CAPRI version); KEPT. Under it the densest regions must cut 76-88% of their surplus (BE25 635 kg/ha -> 88%, NL41 530 -> 86%, BE21, NL21, NL22, BE23), which in the model only herd cuts can deliver - the source of the pig overshoot and the extreme N shadow prices. CAPRI reached pigs -14.5% under the same rule, so its dense regions used relief the model lacks or met the cut differently; which one (manure processing/export, incl. to third countries, p_manureExportsToThirdCountries; low-N feeding; land) needs CAPRI's Farm-to-Fork scenario output to settle.

ammonia_accounting.farm_to_fork: Full 2030 Farm-to-Fork (191 s, 7 iterations; all other results identical - ammonia feeds back into nothing): EU ammonia 2,845 -> 2,306 kt NH3 = -18.9% (proxy: 840 -> 694 kt, -17.4%); CAPRI -33%.
