market_price_transmission.status: REPORTING FIXED; beef base balance inconsistent (next)
market_price_transmission.note: Meat prices under Farm-to-Fork rise far less than CAPRI's (beef +2.6 vs +24%, pork +12.5 vs +43%) because MarketModule.domestic_prices sets every region's price to world price x (1 + tariff): perfect transmission with one world price per commodity, so an EU supply cut moves the EU price only as much as the world price. CAPRI (arm/market_model.gms) has an own producer price per region (SupBalM_, PPri_), a first-stage Armington composite of domestic sales and imports (ArmFit1_, arm2QuantShares_, rho1 = p_rhoArm1, 8.0 by default in arm/market1.gms), bilateral import flows priced at exporter price + transport + tariff (ArmFit2_, impQuant_, impPrice_) and TRQs (TRQImports_). An Armington class exists in the model but never sets prices. armington_params.csv (rho1 beef 3.5, pork 6.7, source 'CAPRI') to be reconciled with CAPRI's 8.0.
market_price_transmission.revision: The model already has CAPRI's EU Armington clearing (MarketModule.eu_armington_premium: two-sided, gross extra-EU trade, first-stage sigma for domestic sales vs imports, second-stage rho2 for exports, bisection, exact at base, bounds 0.67-1.5, applied when gross trade >= 5% of consumption); farmers' price signal = (world x tariff change) x premium. But results report market.domestic_prices for EU27 = world x tariff WITHOUT the premium, and every Farm-to-Fork comparison used that. Producer prices with the premium (2017 base Farm-to-Fork): poultry +19.5% (CAPRI +18%), wheat +9.5% (+8%), milk +1.7% (+1.5%), pork +25.5% (+43%; reported +13.9%), rapeseed +24.1% (+11%: overshoot), beef +5.4% (+24%; premium only x1.024). Elasticities confirmed as CAPRI's effective values (special_ch/market1_ch.gms, included unconditionally after market1.gms's 8.0 default; Fontagne, Guimbard & Orefice 2019). NEXT: report EU producer prices with the premium in market results; re-baseline the CAPRI comparison; then beef (small premium) and the rapeseed overshoot.
market_price_transmission.reporting_fix: MarketEquilibrium.domestic_prices now reports the EU row x the Armington premium (the producer price farmers respond to); world x tariff kept as wedge_prices. Behaviour unchanged (the price signal was already built from world prices x premium). 2030 Farm-to-Fork, producer prices (CAPRI): cereals +10.2% (+8), oilseeds +15.6% (+11), veg+perm +14.0% (+15), poultry +17.0% (+18), milk +1.4% (+1.5), pork +22.9% (+43), beef +4.8% (+24).
market_price_transmission.beef_finding: BEEF: the market's EU base has supply 5,168 kt and demand 3,951 kt (self-sufficiency 131%, net exports 1,217 kt) while gross trade says exports 859 / imports 308 kt (net 551) and FAO's EU27 balance says production 6,905, consumption 6,336 (109%). The premium closes the gap by inflating exports to ~1,525 kt; with rho2 7.1 a small price rise sheds exports, so the premium stays x1.024. Pork and poultry balances are proportionate. NEXT: trace why the EU beef base demand is 38% below FAO's relative to production.

demand_price_reference_bug.note: demand_response took the price ratio as domestic price / BASE WORLD price, so every tariff-protected region's demand was cut by (1 + tariff)^eta at base before any change. EU beef (CAPRI total protection 57.8%, eta -0.4): 1.578^-0.4 = 0.833 - EU base beef use 3,951 kt instead of the aligned 4,742 (FAO self-sufficiency 109% became 131%). The world calibration factor partly hid it for non-EU regions in aggregate, but the EU is exempt from that calibration and kept the error. The inflated EU net exports then absorbed price rises (beef premium x1.024). Fixed: price ratio against the BASE DOMESTIC price (world x base tariff), exactly 1 at base, as the feed-demand terms already did; tariff changes still enter through the domestic price. Anchors 8/8 unchanged; 61/61 tests. Farm-to-Fork 2030 producer prices (CAPRI): beef +4.8 -> +10.3% (+24), pork +22.9 -> +26.4% (+43), poultry +19.0% (+18), veg+perm +15.7% (+15), cereals +10.3% (+8), milk +1.4% (+1.5); quantities within ~1 point.

beef_price_verification.status: market verified; cattle respond at CAPRI elasticities; herd links not the lever - the beef supply gap must come from how Farm-to-Fork instruments act on cattle (not from price responsiveness)
beef_price_verification.note: Hypothesis: EU beef TRQs cap import growth (CAPRI). CAPRI 2030 reference (gd_full): EU beef TrqNT 409.5 kt in total, erga-omnes 191.1 kt with ImportsR 181.5 (95% filled); poultry 53.1 / 52.9 (99.5%); pork 85.1 / 20.8; cheese 83.7 / 16.1; applied out-of-quota tariffs (EU|RW TaAppl BEEF 16.2% + specific); TRQRents BEEF 22.2. Not decisive: the model's EU beef tariff is already CAPRI's total protection (57.8%), i.e. the out-of-quota cost at the margin, and with the quota 95% full extra imports pay exactly that; sigma is the same (3.5). TEST with the model's own premium function, Farm-to-Fork demand: EU beef supply -7.3% (the model's) -> x1.060; -15% -> x1.201; -18% (CAPRI's beef herd cut) -> x1.277, i.e. ~+28% plus the world price change, CAPRI's +24% range. So the beef MARKET is right and the gap is SUPPLY: beef output -7% vs CAPRI herds -18% - herd links (item 2). No TRQ cap built (it would raise the price artificially on top of a correct mechanism). PORK differs: supply already -21% (CAPRI pigs -14.5%) but price +26% (CAPRI +43%); with rho2 13.4 EU pork exports absorb the cut - separate item.

young_animal_links.status: THIRD VERSION (CAPRI's EU market) ON by default (CAPRIModel.use_young_animal_market)
young_animal_links.note: CAPRI ties cattle activities through young-animal balances (supply_model.gms INPANI_): inputs ICAM/ICAF/IBUL/IHEI/ICOW per 1000 head equal outputs YCAM/YCAF/YBUL/YHEI/YCOW. Built per model region (tools/build/build_young_animals.py, 232 regions; DE11: dairy cow 0.81 calves/yr, suckler 0.99; bulls use 1.25 young bulls/place-yr; heifers deliver 0.88 cows; cows need 0.27 replacements; UVAG calf 130, young 591, cow 1,071 EUR). Implemented as three regional balances with base net trade fixed, CAPRI's value as base shadow price and a 0.1% surplus band: base exact (anchors 8/8, fidelity 0.22%), but Farm-to-Fork 2030 did NOT converge (25 iterations, 460 s) and cattle fell LESS (dairy -5.5 -> -2.1%, beef animals -10.3 -> -5.8%; pork and poultry prices jumped). The rigid regional balance forces all cattle activities to shrink together, making any cut costlier; CAPRI has young-animal TRADE between regions (and sales), so a region can sell surplus calves. REVERTED; a faithful version needs that trade (national pool for young animals, as for manure).
young_animal_links.priced_attempt: Young animals as goods traded within each member state at a national price (CAPRI values at base, already in margins; only (p - p0) x net output enters), price per member state cleared by a bracketed search in the outer loop. Germany-only Farm-to-Fork test vs the same run without it: suckler cows -12.6 -> -10.9%, bulls +1.7 -> +2.0%, calves +0.9 -> +0.1% - a small effect; prices moved modestly (calves 130 -> 139, young cattle 591 -> 537 EUR) and the search stalled at a 4.8% imbalance once its bracket went stale. Conclusion: herd linkage, even priced as in CAPRI, does not drive the beef supply gap. LEAD: the registry entry livestock_curvature reads 'FIXED (pigs, poultry); ruminants still damped' - cattle supply responds too weakly. REVERTED.
young_animal_links.capri_market_2026_10_08: CAPRI clears young animals in its MARKET model (arm/market_model.gms yaniMarket_ at market-region level, rmsYaniMarket_ optional per member state): net trade fixed at the reference, prices adjust; the supply models buy and sell them (SUPBAL_ + INPANI_). Implemented: three goods (calves YCAM+YCAF / ICAM+ICAF; young cattle YBUL+YHEI / IBUL+IHEI; cows YCOW / ICOW), one EU price ratio each; margins change by (ratio - 1) x CAPRI base value x (output - input) per head; EU net balance of each good held at the baseline run's level; price update = damped Newton with the supply response approximated from each region's PMP matrix (dx = Q^-1 dc, CAPRI's normalised-quadratic approximation, renewed every outer iteration). DATA FIX: coefficients were per CAPRI head applied to model heads; the model's cattle head counts differ from CAPRI's activity levels (DE11 bulls 5.2 vs 13.1), so EU base balances were far off (young cattle produced 17.4 m vs 5.5 m used). Now per MODEL head = CAPRI regional flow / model heads (as livestock outputs): EU base calves 24.7 vs 24.9 m, young 17.9 vs 20.2, cows 7.2 vs 7.0. Spain: no res_17 dump in the project - earlier per-CAPRI-head coefficients x CAPRI 2030 levels / model heads, UVAG = median of other countries (REGISTERED). Runs: with the literature livestock elasticities the calf price rose x2.9 and cattle fell less; with CAPRI's elasticities calf price +35%, converged in 10 iterations.
young_animal_links.ireland_fix: Irish regions had no young-animal coefficients: national fallback used reg[:2] ('IE') instead of CAPRI's 'IR'; fixed with _model_regions.national_code (235 regions).

farm_to_fork_decomposition.note: Each Farm-to-Fork instrument alone (2017 base, full EU) - beef cattle / dairy cows / pigs / beef producer price / wheat price: landscape 10%: -0.2 / -0.3 / -0.2 / +0.4 / +3.7%; organic 25%: +0.1 / +0.4 / -0.1 / -0.2 / +2.6%; pesticides -50%: -0.1 / +0.5 / -0.5 / -0.2 / +9.8%; N surplus (tiered): -12.8 / -7.0 / -21.9 / +13.4 / -3.8%. Only the nitrogen target moves livestock; the crop instruments raise cereal prices but barely touch ruminants, which feed mainly on own fodder. CAPRI's organic target (pol_input/greendeal/load_organic_targets.gms, set organicCrops: cereals, rice, oilseeds, tomatoes, potatoes, vegetables, pulses, sugar beet, textiles, tobacco, fruit, table grapes/olives/wine) excludes grassland and fodder crops, so in CAPRI too the crop instruments do not cut cattle through fodder (a hypothesis from a cover-crop comment, organic_io.gms line 133, was a misreading). The cattle gap to CAPRI (beef -10.6% vs -18%, dairy -5.4% vs -10% in 2030) therefore lies in how the NITROGEN target bites on cattle regions.

nitrogen_target_regional_pattern.status: done; limit of verification without CAPRI regional F2F output
nitrogen_target_regional_pattern.note: Nitrogen target alone (2017 base): EU cattle -10.7%, mineral N -28.5%, surplus -39.4%. Ten largest cattle regions give 50% of the cattle cut: Ireland IE04/05/06 -40/-30/-35% (N prices 31/36/29), Pays de la Loire -27% (9.0), Brittany -18.5% (42.7), Castilla y Leon -22.8% (7.3), Basse-Normandie -20.1% (14.4); central French grassland regions barely move - Burgundy +1.4% (0.50), Midi-Pyrenees -3.8% (1.31) - meeting a small tiered cut by mineral fertiliser alone (-27 to -29%). Pig regions: North Brabant pigs -85.9% (75.0), Lombardy -65.1% (78.1), Brittany -50.0%, Denmark -36%, Catalonia -27.9% (60.8). ODDITY: Brittany's mineral N RISES +9.7% while its surplus falls 57.6% - to investigate. Whether CAPRI's -18% beef cut comes from the same regions or more broadly needs CAPRI's regional Farm-to-Fork output (not available).
nitrogen_target_regional_pattern.brittany_resolved: Brittany's mineral N 'rise' is land expansion: per ha mineral N 45 -> 44 kg (flat), farmland 1,728 -> 1,957 kha (+13%; wheat 317 -> 598, barley 116 -> 289 kha). Not a bug.
nitrogen_target_regional_pattern.land_abandonment_loophole: Under the nitrogen target farmland COLLAPSES in livestock regions: Lombardy 1,026 -> 577 kha (-44%, every crop falls), North Brabant 247 -> 173 (-30%), Ireland IE05 2,208 -> 1,687 (-24%). The model's constraint caps the TOTAL surplus (target per ha x BASE farmland), so for any crop whose fertiliser exceeds its uptake, abandoning land lowers the total surplus - a loophole. CAPRI's constraint is per ha of CURRENT land (supply_model.gms e_SURTOTHa/e_EXCRET), where abandoning land does not help; but adopting it here earlier produced the opposite extreme (Lombardy farmland +62%), because a hectare's dilution is worth far more than land costs at the model's N shadow prices (EUR 30-80/kg in livestock regions). Both extremes, like the unfed-maize and manure-sink episodes, trace to those shadow prices. The open question is why cutting the surplus is so costly in the model's livestock regions.
nitrogen_target_regional_pattern.excretion_check: Suspect 'CAPRI animals excrete less through feeding' REJECTED: CAPRI's manure N per head is DATA(MAACT,'MANN') (fixed), times (1 - gaseous losses); feeding enters only through mitigation options (lowNFeed, rumFedEff, mlkYld) under %ghgAbatement% == on (supply_model.gms manExportOrAppl_), which the main Farm-to-Fork scenario very likely did not use. OPEN DEFINITIONAL CHECK: CAPRI's surplus (e_SURTOTHa, e_EXCRET) counts manure NET of gaseous losses (v_ManureNPK, 'net of gaseous losses'); if the model counts manure gross, livestock regions carry larger surpluses and the tiered rule asks larger cuts. North Brabant totals matched (530 vs 531 kg/ha) but its manure term did not (612 vs CAPRI EXCRET 568).
nitrogen_target_regional_pattern.gross_net_check: No gross/net mismatch: across 153 regions, model (2017 base) / CAPRI (2030 reference) per ha - manure term median 1.04 (10th 0.62, 90th 1.21), mineral fertiliser 1.21 (0.92-1.57), surplus 1.06 (0.68-1.55). A gross-vs-net difference would show as ~1.2-1.3 on manure everywhere. Notable: mineral N 21% above CAPRI's, and wide regional scatter in surplus, which matters because the tiered rule cuts high surpluses hardest.

nitrogen_target_root_cause.status: CLOSED for this phase: market and per-ha form complete, converging, tested; OFF by default on evidence
nitrogen_target_root_cause.note: WHY the model cannot behave like CAPRI under the N-surplus target. CAPRI's supply model (supply_model.gms NUTNED_, fertDistMine_, fertDistExcr_) allocates fertiliser endogenously: per crop group, need = data x v_cropNutNeedMultFact (+ v_cropNutNeedAddFact) x sqrt(yield factor) is covered by mineral N x (1 - losses) + manure N x v_nutAvailFactExcr + residues. In simulation the three factors are FIXED at calibrated values (supply_model_thread_load_or_unload_values_constant_over_iter.gms; .fx in set_miti_bounds.gms, aggreg.gms) - over-fertilisation is NOT a free lever. What CAPRI has and the model lacks is the SUBSTITUTION itself: mineral N = need - availability x manure - residues (>= 0). The model's N row is linear with each crop's mineral N fixed per ha regardless of manure (_balance_coefs evaluates each activity alone), so manure never replaces fertiliser. Consequences: (1) in dense pig regions CAPRI's mineral N is near zero, so EXPORTING manure cuts the surplus one-for-one; (2) in low-livestock regions IMPORTING manure replaces mineral N, raising the surplus only by the unavailable share and SAVING fertiliser cost - willing importers - so CAPRI's manure pool clears at moderate prices; (3) in the model an importer's surplus rises one-for-one with no saving, so the pool cleared only at EUR 58-98/kg N, and without trade dense regions can only cut herds -> extreme N shadow prices (EUR 30-80/kg), land abandonment (Lombardy -44%) or, with per-ha current land, massive expansion (+62%), unfed silage maize, and pigs -22% vs CAPRI -14.5%. PLAN: (a) fertiliser allocation in the regional QP: mineral N as a variable, >= sum(crop need x area) - availability x manure applied - residues, >= 0, with CAPRI's regional availability (data: fertiliser_substitution_2030.csv) and fertiliser cost; calibrated so the base is exact; (b) then re-enable the national manure pool (built and tested earlier); (c) then CAPRI's per-ha-of-current-land surplus form.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.stage1_attempt1: Implemented in the land-market augmentation: mineral N variable M >= sum(crop base mineral N + manure-covered need spread by uptake) x area - availability x manure (CAPRI availability, fertiliser_substitution_2030.csv), N row with M instead of fixed crop mineral N, fertiliser charged at CAPRI UVAG NITF (new mineral_n_price.csv: AT 869, BG 443, BL 1,035 EUR/t; median 1,032), base-dual shifts. Test (8 regions, nitrogen target only): results moved the WRONG way - pigs Lombardy -78% (was -69), North Brabant -95% (-88), Brittany -73% (-55); cattle -30 to -43%; mineral N -60%; reported N shadow prices all zero. Expected the opposite (substitution makes herd cuts costlier). Suspects: (1) the N row's crop coefficients are not plain base mineral N - they are scaled by the fertiliser-intensity response to the N price, so subtracting full base mineral N leaves crops absorbing N they do not; (2) shadow-price reporting does not read the augmented solve, hiding what the problem does. REVERTED. Next: read how the N row is assembled per solve (intensity terms), redesign the allocation on that basis, and report the augmented duals before testing.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.stage1_attempt2: Re-implemented with crops' CURRENT mineral N (base x fertiliser intensity x sqrt(yield ratio), the same terms as the N row) and with the augmented problem kept so the N row's shadow price can be recovered (NNLS on active rows at the solution). Same results as attempt 1, so double counting was NOT the cause. The visible shadow prices show the target gets HARDER with substitution (Burgundy 0.5 -> 12.9, Duesseldorf 3.2 -> 23.1, Brittany 47 -> 78; pigs Lombardy -64 -> -78%, Brittany -50 -> -73%): when manure replaces fertiliser, a head cut relieves only the unavailable share of its manure (availability ~0.44), so more heads must go. That is CAPRI's own economics; CAPRI's relief comes from the MANURE MARKET that substitution makes work (importers replace fertiliser and save its cost). Stage 1 is therefore correct but must not be on without stage 2. Kept behind use_fert_allocation = False; default results unchanged (61/61 tests, anchors 8/8).
nitrogen_target_root_cause.stage2: National manure market working THROUGH the allocation: per region extra exports/imports of manure N (N row -1/+1; allocation row +a/-a, so importers save fertiliser; manure-application row -1/+1; CAPRI quadratic cost +50 EUR/t per extra 1% of regional manure traded; exports <= manure produced); pool price per member state by bracketed search in the outer loop; pool clearing in the convergence test. Test, nitrogen target only, IT+NL+DK+FR: pigs (4 countries) neither -41.0%, allocation only -55.4%, allocation + market -38.0%. Works where countries have dense AND sparse regions: Brittany pigs -48.5 -> -5.0% (exports 159 kt N), Lombardy -62 -> -28% (68 kt), Burgundy imports 28 kt; N shadow prices Brittany 48 -> 20, Lombardy 84 -> 46. Fails where all regions are dense: North Brabant -85 -> -94%, Denmark -33 -> -51% (pool prices NL 86, DK 51 kEUR/t) - CAPRI also lets manure leave the country (processing, p_manureExportsToThirdCountries), not modelled. Not converged in 20 iterations (pool imbalance 5.4%). Cattle -12.4 -> -22.9% with the allocation (own-grassland manure interaction to check). Default unchanged (61/61 tests, anchors 8/8).
nitrogen_target_root_cause.stage3_design: CROSS-BORDER MANURE (what NL and DK lack): CAPRI's manure market (manuremarket/declare_manure_market.gms, define_manure_market_structure.gms) has ONE POOL PER COUNTRY and EVERY PAIR OF POOLS CONNECTED: v_mPoolExports(pool1, pool2) at trade cost p_mPoolTradeCost = (1 EUR loading + 0.18 EUR/t/km x distance, Van der Straeten et al. 2010) per t fresh manure, converted to pure nutrient with mean content 7.97% (cattle 4.95, pigs 6.91, poultry 15.89, other 4.14) - e.g. ~0.69 EUR/kg N at 300 km. Pool clearing (e_mPoolClear): net exports to other pools = pool excess supply - FIXED exports to third countries (p_manureExportsToThirdCountries, data, not a flexible outlet). Distance between pools = distance between their centre NUTS-2 regions (rManPool_centre) from nuts2_center_distance (%datdir%/fert/nuts2_center_distance.gdx, metres/1000) - DATA REQUESTED from the project lead.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.stage3: Connected pools implemented (CAPRIModel._update_manure_pools, runs only with use_manure_market): 34 country pools, 930 pairs from CAPRI's distance matrix (NL->DE 227 km = EUR 525/t N), Takayama-Judge spatial equilibrium each iteration with local secant slopes. Test (N target; IT, NL, DK, FR, DE, BE/LU): prices became joint (EUR 5.7-9.7/kg vs 51-86 in closed NL/DK pools) but NOT converged in 25 iterations: EVERY region exports and NONE imports, the plan sends manure to BL (NL 351, IT 201, DK 114 kt N) that no Belgian region takes; planned vs realised gap 4x supply. The resulting pigs -11.8% is meaningless (bottomless sink). NEXT: find what blocks imports - importers' own N targets (tiered rule binds everywhere) or the 170 kg/ha manure-application limit capping the import column.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.stage3_correction: CORRECTION of the stage-3 reading: imports DO happen. With the pool price fixed at 9 kEUR/t N (FR, BE, DE): Burgundy imports 27.8 kt N, Centre 28.5, Brandenburg 10.1. Reduced-cost decomposition of the import variable: price -p; N row +mu_N; allocation row -a x mu_alloc, where mu_alloc = fertiliser price + mu_N (mineral N counts in the surplus too); so a region imports once p covers (1 - a) mu_N - a p_f. Importers' own N shadow prices are EUR 5-37/kg (Burgundy 18.8, BE33 37.5) because the tiered rule binds everywhere, so the pool clears only at EUR 6-10/kg. 'No region imports' came from listing only exporting regions. The real failure was the price SEARCH: secant slopes with a -0.5 x supply default gave plans 4x supply away from the regions' responses. Replaced by the ANALYTIC slope from the regional KKT conditions (-1/s per active trade side, s = 0.05/(supply/100): 20% of supply per kEUR/t). To test next.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.stage3_test2: With the analytic slope (same six countries, N target, 25 iterations): planned-vs-realised gap 4.04 -> 2.29 x supply, pool prices creeping up ~0.04 kEUR/t per iteration (BE 8.1, FR 11.3, IT 12.2, DE 12.4, NL 12.4, DK 13.1 kEUR/t), not converged. Regional responses have kinks (regions switch between importing, exporting and not trading), so local slopes mislead. NEXT: replace the linearised pool step by an exact formulation - e.g. solve the pool equilibrium on the regions' actual reduced-cost thresholds (each region's import/export threshold prices are known from its KKT terms), or a bracketed search per pool on net exports with inter-pool arbitrage enforced afterwards.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.stage3_exact: Exact-schedule clearing implemented (_update_manure_pools): per region, threshold prices for exporting/importing from the reduced costs of its trade variables at the solution (multipliers by NNLS on the active rows); pool net-export schedules with their kinks; connected equilibrium as the dual of the Takayama-Judge problem (min sum Phi_k(p_k) s.t. p_k - p_l <= c_kl, Phi closed form). Two bugs found and fixed on the way: a region's stored problem could predate its market columns (guarded); the export cap was read from the last row, which is the grassland row (now manure produced at the solution). Last test (six countries): prices stayed at 0 and the 'gap' fell to 0 - NOT a solution: SLSQP did not succeed on the kinked objective (prices kept), and the convergence metric compares realised exports with the plan, not pool CLEARING. NEXT: (1) convergence must require every pool to clear (|net exports - net shipments| / supply < 1%); (2) solve the dual price problem with a method that handles the kinks - e.g. the primal QP in shipments with the exact piecewise-linear schedules as breakpoint-segment variables, solved by the model's own QP solver.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.stage3_primal: Primal spatial equilibrium on the exact regional schedules (regional exports/imports + inter-pool shipments, pool balance, CAPRI costs), solved by the model's active-set QP from the all-zero (always feasible) start, exact least-distance as fallback; the shipment ridge scaled to 1e-3 x the smallest regional slope (a 1e-6 ridge made the least-distance method misread ill-conditioning as infeasibility). Convergence now requires pool CLEARING (realised net exports = planned net shipments). Six-country test (N target): every iteration solves; prices joint, spreads = transport costs (FR lowest, DK highest); clearing gap 0.95 -> 0.62 -> 0.43 -> 0.26 -> 0.16 -> 0.10 -> 0.06 -> 0.031 after 25 iterations, prices still rising (~EUR 17-18/kg N). Not yet within 1%: needs more iterations or acceleration. The price level reflects the tiered rule binding in every region, importers included.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.stage3_convergence: Pool price steps: over-relaxation (x1.5 per same-direction step, max 3x) while the clearing gap > 10%, damped (0.5) below. Six-country test: gap 0.952 -> 0.091 by iteration 7 (was 13), then a steady decline 0.052 -> 0.028 by iteration 25 without the oscillation (2.8-4.7%) that over-relaxation alone produced. By pool after 12 iterations: DK 0.1%, DE 0.6%, NL 1.3%, FR 1.9%, BL 2.1%, IT 4.6% of manure supply; residual from regional N shadow prices shifting with trade (schedules one iteration stale). Results insensitive to the residual: pigs -18.0% and cattle -18.9% in both the oscillating and the damped run. Reaching 1% needs ~30 more iterations; decision pending: tolerance vs iterations.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.tolerance: Manure-market convergence tolerance parameterised: CAPRIModel.manure_pool_tolerance (share of each pool's manure supply), default 0.03, chosen by the project lead after the six-country test showed results stable at that level. Only used with use_manure_market. Note: the outer loop's iteration cap (max_outer_iter, default 25) may need raising for tighter tolerances.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.full_eu_run_1: ProjectionModule.CARRIED_SETTINGS now includes use_manure_market and manure_pool_tolerance (without them the 2030 model would silently run without the market, as happened earlier with the ration). First full-EU 2030 Farm-to-Fork with the market on (3% tolerance): 858 s for baseline + scenario (market off ~3 min); NOT converged within the 25-iteration cap. Comparison invalid: the saved market-off result had been overwritten by the reverted herd-links experiment. Reported EU N surplus only -21% (target implies ~-37 to -40%): suspected because the environmental accounting recomputes manure from herds and FIXED base trade shares, so endogenous pool exports/imports are invisible in the reported surplus. Cereal price +30% to explain. NEXT: (1) reported N balance must include the endogenous manure trade; (2) re-run market-off comparator; (3) raise the iteration cap for market runs (e.g. 40).
nitrogen_target_root_cause.check3: CONSISTENCY CHECK (six countries, market on, 8 iterations): every region's own N row meets its target EXACTLY (105/105), but the reported surplus is higher - median ratio reported/own-row 1.43 (10th 1.19, 90th 1.94) - so only 1 region meets its target in the report. Largest gaps roughly equal the region's manure EXPORTS (Lombardy own row 67.9 kt, reported 153.2 kt, exports 82.3 kt). The regional results DO carry the trade and allocated mineral N (ITC4 export 82.3 kt, M 92.7 kt; FRC1 import 60.2 kt), and the table is built through compute_indicators (patched). So either later code in compute_indicators overrides the adjusted n_surplus, or inner-loop re-solves replace some result objects before the trade is attached (attached after the FIRST solve only). Working-copy changes (reporting, iteration cap) are untested by the suite and NOT packaged; the 17:17 package remains the valid one.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.check3_decomposition: Lombardy, Italy-only run, market on: OWN ROW = crops -70,932 (= -uptake 84,559 + fixation 6,453 + deposition 7,173) + animals +126,325 + M 120,869 - exports 108,334 = 67,927 = target. REPORTED = mineral 120,869 (= M, correct) + organic 107,325 (= 215,659 own manure - 108,334 exports, correct) + fixation 6,453 + deposition 7,173 - uptake 84,559 = 157,261; animal products 53,915 listed but NOT subtracted. So the trade/allocation adjustment WORKS; the two balances differ in (1) organic input: the full balance counts ~89 kt more manure N (215,659) than the sum of the per-activity animal terms (126,325) - area-related organic terms (e.g. the fixed base manure trade per ha) that per-activity evaluation never captures; (2) definition: the reported surplus = inputs - crop uptake, while the row's animal terms appear net of animal products. IMPLICATION: the row is built the same way with the market OFF, so the reported N surplus may never have matched what regions meet - including the -40.5% EU Farm-to-Fork result. NEXT: run the same check with the market OFF; then align the row with the reported (CAPRI SURTOT) definition.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.correction_substitution: MARKET OFF consistency check (six countries): reported / own-row surplus median 1.000 (10th 0.976, 90th 1.000); all 105 regions meet the target in the report too - the default model's reporting is consistent and the -40.5% EU result stands. Lombardy's row animal term 126,325 t ~ (1 - availability 0.44) x manure 215,659 t: the environmental balance ALREADY applies manure-mineral substitution linearly with CAPRI's availability factors (fertiliser_substitution_2030.csv), and the per-activity row captures it in the animal coefficients. The earlier diagnosis 'manure never replaces fertiliser in the model' was WRONG. Stage 1 (fertiliser allocation) therefore DOUBLE-COUNTS substitution - the source of the market-on mismatch (reported 43% above the row). REDESIGN: drop the allocation; give the manure-market columns coefficients consistent with the existing linear substitution - N row -(1 - a) per t exported, +(1 - a) per t imported (1 where mineral N is at its floor), and the fertiliser saving/cost a x p_f in the objective (importers save, exporters pay), so importers have the incentive CAPRI's market rests on.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.redesign: Allocation removed from the market path (RegionalSupplyModel.use_fert_allocation forced False). Market columns now use the balance's own linear substitution: N row -(1 - a)/+(1 - a) per t exported/imported; objective: exporters pay pool price + a x p_f, importers receive pool price + a x p_f; manure-application row +-1; CAPRI quadratic cost; exports <= manure produced. Reporting: traded manure enters with organic +-1, mineral -+a, surplus +-(1 - a); allocation override removed. Consistency check, market ON (six countries, 8 iterations): reported / own-row median 1.000 (10th 1.000, 90th 1.001); 102 of 105 regions on target in the report; outliers West Flanders BE25 +29%, Antwerp BE21 +12% - mineral N at its floor there, so traded manure should count fully (registered simplification). Trade flowing: ITC4 exports 112 kt N, FRC1 imports 75 kt. 61/61 tests, anchors 8/8 (market off by default).
nitrogen_target_root_cause.floor: Market columns now use the balance's exact substitution factor (availability / mineral efficiency, EnvironmentalModule._substitution - not availability alone) and its floor: where the region's mineral N is zero at the current solution, traded manure counts in full with no fertiliser cost/saving; the regional result carries the factor used (0 at the floor) and the report applies the same. Consistency check, market on (six countries): reported / own-row median 1.000, 10th 1.000, 90th 1.000; ALL 105 regions on target in the report (West Flanders and Antwerp fixed). 61/61 tests.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.solver: Pool equilibrium now solved by an interior-point (Newton) method: capri_mod/supply/convex_qp.solve_convex_qp - Clarabel (Apache-2.0, optional dependency 'solvers': pip install clarabel) when installed, else a built-in dense primal-dual method with Mehrotra predictor-corrector; pool balances as TRUE equalities. Test on 40 random strictly convex QPs: interior point solved 39, the active-set loop 15 (iteration limit; singular KKT systems from equalities written as tight inequality pairs); where both solved, max relative difference 6e-6; IPM median 10 Newton steps. FULL EU (2017 base, Farm-to-Fork, market on): manure vanishing into uncleared pools 2.41 Mt N -> 160 kt (iteration 1) -> 30 kt (iteration 6, 0.4% of EU manure). The worst-pool measure stays ~0.35-0.39, entirely from small peripheral pools: Malta (3 kt supply), Cyprus (26 kt), Lithuania, Latvia. 61/61 tests. Market still off by default.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.dual_prices: Pool prices now = shadow prices (multipliers) of the pool balance equations, returned by both solvers (Clarabel sol.z; built-in IPM y). For an exporting region s e - th_e + y_k = 0, so y_k = th_e - s e, the price definition, available for EVERY pool. Toy check: exporter th 5, importer th 1, slopes 1 -> trade 2, multiplier 3 (exact). Previously prices came from actively trading regions only, so pools whose regions did not trade kept stale prices (Malta, Cyprus, Lithuania, Latvia stuck at 35-39%). Full EU, 6 iterations: worst pool gap 0.144 -> 0.076 -> 0.067 -> 0.063 -> 0.059 -> 0.058 (Norway; all others <= ~3.3%). BUT manure unaccounted across pools 200 kt (2.4% of EU manure) at iteration 6 vs 30 kt with the previous price rule, falling slowly - to watch in the full run. 61/61 tests.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.full_eu_run_3: Convergence test now also requires EU-wide conservation (|sum of realised net exports into pools| / EU manure supply <= tolerance); the model keeps a per-iteration trace (_pool_trace) and the projection keeps its last projected model for diagnostics. Full-EU 2030 Farm-to-Fork, market on: 452 s (was 1,368), NOT converged in 40 - worst pool 5.1% -> 4.3% and EU unaccounted 2.0% -> 1.5% over the last 12 iterations (~0.07 points/iteration). Results vs market off (CAPRI): pigs -21.7 -> -12.9% (-14.5), sheep -5.5 -> -10.6% (-9.5), beef price +10.3 -> +24.9% (+24), poultry price +17.2% (+18), non-CO2 GHG -11.9 -> -16.0% (-14.8), N surplus -40.0%; but beef animals -25.4% (-18), dairy -3.9% (-10), cereal price +34.9% (+8), cereal production -24.3% (-15) - crops overshoot. Not converged, so provisional. NEXT: tail convergence (damping 0.5 near the solution is slow), then the crop overshoot.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.full_eu_converged: Adaptive damping replaced the fixed half step (full step while the gap falls, x1.25 per fall capped at 1, halved to min 0.25 when it rises). The tail contraction is set by the regional schedules shifting with prices (~3.5% of the gap per iteration), not by damping. manure_max_outer_iter default 60. FULL-EU 2030 Farm-to-Fork, market on: CONVERGED in 57 iterations, 615 s for baseline + scenario; final worst pool 2.9%, EU unaccounted 0.6%. Results identical to the 40-iteration run to 0.1 point (stable): pigs -12.9% (CAPRI -14.5), sheep -10.5% (-9.5), beef price +24.8% (+24), poultry price +17.2% (+18), non-CO2 GHG -16.0% (-14.8); beef animals -25.4% (-18), dairy -3.9% (-10), cereal price +34.9% (+8), cereal production -24.3% (-15). NEXT: the crop overshoot. 61/61 tests.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.crop_overshoot: CROP OVERSHOOT DIAGNOSED (2017 base, full EU, Farm-to-Fork; market off converged in 8, market on NOT converged in 60): EU cereal area off -5.3%, on -26.4%. 137 IMPORTING regions: cereal area off -5.1%, on -31.4%; their median N shadow price 0.47 -> 15.8 EUR/kg. 88 exporters: -5.9 -> -18.8%, shadow price 18.7 -> 19.3. 23 non-trading: -5.3 -> +3.7%. Mechanism: importers are PAID the pool price (~EUR 15-19/kg N, set by the exporters' extreme shadow prices) per t of manure taken - far more than cereals earn per kg N - so they import until their own target binds hard and shrink crops to fit more paid manure in. Root again: the exporters' N shadow prices (~EUR 19/kg). CAPRI's pool prices are presumably far lower (p_manurePoolPrice default 0.5) - to check how CAPRI limits imports: e.g. manure applied within crop nutrient need (fertDistExcr_), import cost slope, or the price calibration term (v_mPoolPriceCal).
nitrogen_target_root_cause.capri_import_limits: How CAPRI limits manure imports (checking): (a) trade costs as ours - buy/sell slope 50/(own manure supply/100) EUR/t, constants calibrated so each region's base trade status (importer/exporter/autarky, from p_dualValueManureCal vs base pool price) is optimal; manure has a POSITIVE base pool price (~EUR 0.5/kg, fertiliser value) that importers pay - not the decisive difference. (b) fertDistExcr_: ALL manure incl. imports must be distributed to crop groups (v_fertDist 'Excr' >= 0), and NUTNED_ counts it at availability with mineral >= 0 - if NUTNED_ is an equality, manure is capped by crop nutrient need, so cutting crops REDUCES an importer's capacity (the opposite of the model, whose only application limit is 170 kg N/ha). Form of NUTNED_ recorded below.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.env_module_bug: BUG FOUND: the environmental module lived only on SupplyModule (_env_for_surplus); regional models had none, so every regional call to its substitution factor raised AttributeError inside a try/except. Consequences: (1) the crop-need limit (CAPRI NUTNED_ =E= with mineral >= 0; manure within crop need) was silently skipped - the comparison after adding it was identical to every decimal; (2) the manure market silently used plain availability instead of the balance's factor (availability / efficiency x share of need above CAPRI's minimum-mineral floor) and its floor check never ran - e.g. North Brabant true 0.030 vs fallback ~0.20, Duesseldorf 0.257 vs ~0.37, Burgundy 0.429 vs ~0.62; the consistency check still passed because the report used the same fallback. FIX: SupplyModule passes its environmental module to each regional model (created once if missing); fallbacks now emit warnings. Verified on DE11, NL41, FRC1: module present, crop-need row added (14 -> 15 rows), no fallback warnings. 61/61 tests, anchors 8/8. All market results since the 'exact substitution' step must be re-run. Housekeeping noted: several loaders leave data files unclosed.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.rerun_after_env_fix: Crop comparison re-run with the correct substitution factors and the crop-need limit active (2017 base, Farm-to-Fork): EU cereal area market off -5.3%, on -25.3% (was -26.4%); 145 importers -5.1 -> -28.9%, median N shadow price 0.48 -> 16.3 EUR/kg; 80 exporters -5.9 -> -20.2%, shadow price 27.9 (off) -> 20.1 (on). Market-on still NOT converged in 60 iterations (imports 1.72 Mt N vs exports 1.26 Mt). The crop-need limit does not bind in importers (their own N target does), so it cannot stop the crop-for-manure-fee trade. Everything traces to the exporters' N shadow prices (EUR 20-28/kg). NEW LEAD: JRC121368's EU surplus fell 33.5% while the tiered rule applied in full implies ~37.5%, so CAPRI did not fully meet its targets - if CAPRI imposes the target with a slack and a PENALTY (soft constraint), the penalty caps the shadow price, explaining both moderate manure prices and the shortfall. To check in surptot.gms / supply_model.gms (slack variable on the MAXS bound and its objective penalty).
nitrogen_target_root_cause.penalty_lead: LEAD REJECTED: CAPRI's Farm-to-Fork surplus limit is a HARD constraint - supply_model.gms SURTOT_REST_: v_nutSurTot(RUNR,'NITF') =L= MAXS x 1000 (kg/ha), no slack or penalty anywhere. The model's hard constraint matches. The JRC121368 EU result (-33.5%) vs the ~-37.5% implied by the tiered rule on the MODEL's base surpluses may come from (1) CAPRI applying the rule to its own 2030 baseline surpluses (regional ratio model/CAPRI 0.68-1.55), or (2) CAPRI's per-ha-of-CURRENT-land form with its land market, letting farmland expansion dilute the per-ha surplus. (2) was tested earlier (farmland Lombardy +62%) but BEFORE the correct substitution factors, the crop-need limit and the land-market scale fix - worth re-testing.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.baseline_severity: Tiered cut on the model's base surplus vs on CAPRI's 2030 surplus, densest regions: NL41 530 vs 531 kg/ha (85.9% both), NL21 81.1 vs 80.1%, NL22 80.9 vs 79.4%, MT00, CY00 within ~1 point; NL31/NL13/NL12/NL11 LESS demanding in the model (63 vs 76% etc.). Explanation 'CAPRI applies the rule to different baseline surpluses' REJECTED for the dense regions.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.full_eu_run_after_env_fix: Full-EU 2030 Farm-to-Fork, market on, correct substitution factors + crop-need limit: completed in 717 s, NOT converged in 60 - worst pool ~12.5% and EU unaccounted ~5.5%, FLAT over the last iterations (a stall, not slow convergence; before the fixes it converged at 57). Results (market off -> on; CAPRI): pigs -21.7 -> -14.1 (-14.5), poultry -12.3 -> -10.2 (-16.5), sheep -5.5 -> -11.4 (-9.5), beef animals -10.3 -> -26.0 (-18), dairy -5.5 -> -4.4 (-10), beef price +26.0 (+24), poultry price +18.5 (+18), pork price +13.3 (+43), cereal price +35.1 (+8), cereal production -24.5 (-15), fertiliser N2O -38.7 (-40.4), non-CO2 GHG -16.8 (-14.8). Memory not an issue (process ~240 MB of 4 GB); the earlier stopped run remains unexplained. NEXT: which pools stall and why (the crop-need row may make some regions' import/export schedules infeasible or kinked), then the per-ha-of-current-land re-test.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.stall_diagnosis: STALL DIAGNOSED (2017 base, full EU, market on, 16 iterations): EU-wide realised net exports into the pools ~ -230 to -260 kt N every iteration; worst pools all NEGATIVE (realised net exports below plan): Italy -10%, Estonia -8%, Finland -7%, Lithuania -6.5%, Sweden -6.7%; worst gap flat ~0.10-0.13. Cause: each region's schedule assumes its trade moves by 1/s per unit of price (s = trade-cost slope), but with the N target binding the region's own N shadow price shifts as it trades (an exporter loosens its constraint and its incentive weakens), so realised responses are smaller than planned and prices move too little. Before the substitution fix the factors happened to mask this. NEXT: quasi-Newton (Broyden-type) correction per pool - scale each pool's schedule slopes by realised / planned response from the previous iteration.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.quasi_newton: Per-pool response factor kappa (Broyden-type: realised / planned change in net exports, clipped 0.05-1.5) scales each pool's regional schedules (slope s/kappa, re-anchored at current trade). 2017 base full EU: converged in 12 iterations (worst pool 0.7%, EU unaccounted 30 kt) vs no convergence in 60. FULL-EU 2030 Farm-to-Fork: converged in 17 iterations, <295 s for baseline + scenario; worst pool 0.8%, EU unaccounted 0.3%. Results (market off -> on; CAPRI): sheep -5.5 -> -9.8 (-9.5), pigs -21.7 -> -12.3 (-14.5), beef price +10.3 -> +23.9 (+24), poultry price +19.0 -> +15.4 (+18), non-CO2 GHG -11.9 -> -15.4 (-14.8), beef animals -24.5 (-18), dairy -3.8 (-10), poultry -8.9 (-16.5), pork price +11.0 (+43), cereal price +32.9 (+8), cereal production -23.0 (-15). 61/61 tests.
nitrogen_target_root_cause.decision: Per-ha-of-current-land form (CAPRI e_SURTOTHa) added as CAPRIModel.surplus_per_current_ha (default False). Full-EU 2030 Farm-to-Fork, market on + per-ha: converged in 14; N surplus -35.2% (CAPRI -33.5), beef animals -20.8 (-18), cereal price +28.4 (+8). Mean absolute deviation vs JRC121368 over 20 indicators (all / prices / herds / crops / environment): market off 4.4 / 5.6 / 5.5 / 0.7 / 3.7; market on 6.5 / 10.6 / 4.6 / 6.0 / 2.9; market on + per-ha 6.5 / 11.1 / 5.2 / 4.1 / 2.8. DECISION: market-off remains the default (closest to CAPRI overall); manure market (use_manure_market) and per-ha form are available settings. KNOWN LIMITATION with the market on: manure-importing regions give up crops for manure fees (cereal price ~+30% vs +8%), because exporters' N shadow prices (EUR 20-28/kg) set high manure prices; CAPRI's dense regions face the same tiered cuts, so the remaining difference lies elsewhere (open).
nitrogen_target_root_cause.market_default_attempt: Bringing the manure market in (project lead's request). (1) CAPRI per-crop N in its 2030 reference: soft wheat, Burgundy (FR260000): NITF 180 kg/ha, NMIN 93.5, NMAN 78.7 (manure on arable at scale), yield 7.2 t/ha. Model, wheat alone in FRC1: mineral need 133.7, deposition 14.6, uptake 136.3 -> net surplus contribution only +13.6 kg/ha, so crops are NOT heavily penalised per ha. (2) The crop cut in importers is driven by the manure FEE: a hectare of wheat given up frees ~13.6/(1-0.43) = 24 kg of importable manure N, ~EUR 380/ha at the pool price (~EUR 16/kg), more than cereals earn; CAPRI's base pool price is ~EUR 0.5/kg. (3) CAPRI's pool price calibration term v_mPoolPriceCal is a FIXED wedge set in the baseline (e_mPoolPriceCal, e_mPoolObjeCal), not a damping of price changes - ruled out. (4) Remaining candidate: CAPRI's regional linear excess-supply slopes p_mPoolSupSlope ('calibrated slope of the excess supply', e_mPoolSurplus) - if far flatter than the model's (trade-cost slope x quasi-Newton factor), CAPRI's pool prices settle far lower. Its assignment is outside declare_manure_market.gms - to locate (simu_manure_market.gms / calibration).
nitrogen_target_root_cause.pool_slope: CAPRI's regional excess-supply slope in the pool model (manuremarket/declare_manure_market.gms ~l.492): p_mPoolSupSlope = p_manPointSupElas (0.01, 'manure is a by-product ... depends much more on the value of the primary output') x manure supply / calibrated manure dual value; the constant is refitted each iteration to the supply models' net position and value (simu_manure_market.gms). The pool model's slopes shape only the ITERATION PATH: at convergence both CAPRI and the model satisfy the same conditions (regions optimal at pool prices, pools cleared at transport costs), so the slopes cannot explain different equilibrium manure prices. The difference must lie in the regional supply models - how costly exporting regions find cutting their surplus (N shadow prices EUR 20-28/kg) - which cannot be settled without CAPRI's regional Farm-to-Fork output. CONCLUSION for the default question: the manure market and the per-ha form stay optional; candidates exhausted from code alone.

jrc121368_report.note: JRC121368 itself (Barreiro-Hurle et al. 2021). (1) Table 17: CAPRI's Farm-to-Fork run INCLUDES endogenous mitigation technologies (adoption baseline -> combined): precision farming 0 -> 35%, nitrification inhibitors 0 -> 18%, cover storage of manure 14 -> 34%, air purification in housing 0 -> 10%, higher milk yield 0 -> 15%, higher ruminant efficiency 5 -> 9%, nitrate additive 0 -> 7%, catch crops 23 -> 32%, fallowing peatlands 2 -> 9%, anaerobic digestion 2 -> 4%, low-emission housing 12 -> 12%; LOW-NITROGEN FEED 0 -> 0. Corrects the earlier assumption that its mitigation module was off; plausibly explains the ammonia gap (-19 vs -33%) and part of enteric methane and cattle. (2) Figure 8 (p. 49) maps regional changes: N surplus in the Netherlands, Brittany and other dense regions in the darkest class (-36% to -104%), but a few regions RED (surplus rises, up to +103%): western Germany near the Dutch border, Aquitaine, Austria, lower Danube - their targets evidently do not bind, so they can absorb manure freely. In the model every region's tiered target binds. (3) Table 11: the nutrient target is applied at regional level; the exact rule (footnote 3 and text) still to read - it may exempt or treat low-surplus regions differently. NEXT: read Table 11's footnotes and the target description; then implement CAPRI's mitigation technologies inside the supply model.

jrc_nine_region_cap.note: JRC121368 sect. 4.3.4 (p. 23): the tiered target 'for nine regions with high GNB values in the baseline associated with high animal numbers generated infeasibilities ... the reduction target for these regions were set at the EU average (36%)'. Implemented in SupplyModule (JRC_CAPPED_N_REGIONS = 9, JRC_CAPPED_CUT = 0.36); the nine are taken as the highest CAPRI baseline surplus per ha (the report does not name them - REGISTERED reading): BE25 560, NL41 539, BE21 464, NL21 387, NL22 377, NL31 321, BE23 316, NL42 302, MT00 274 kg N/ha. 2030 Farm-to-Fork, market off: pigs -21.7 -> -15.7% (CAPRI -14.5), N surplus -40.5 -> -37.9 (-33.5), manure CH4 -14.5 -> -10.9 (-12.2), pork price +26.4 -> +15.5 (+43), GHG -11.9 -> -9.9 (-14.8). Mean absolute deviation over 20 indicators: market off 4.4 -> 5.1 (prices 5.6 -> 7.9), market on 6.5 -> 6.6; market on still overshoots crops (cereal price +31.8%). Kept on fidelity grounds (CAPRI's own implementation); the remaining price gap points to the missing mitigation technologies (report Table 17). 61/61 tests.

capri_manure_market_in_jrc121368.note: JRC121368 ran WITHOUT manure trade: p. 24 'the model assumes that all manure generated in a region has to be used within that region ... the GNB for these regions is overestimated and impacts on animal numbers would be lower for them were we able to capture the trade in manure'; p. 18 lists 'lack of data on manure imports and exports'. The current CAPRI code has the market as an option (manureTradeNew = %New_Manure_Trade_fromGUI%, capmod/set_global_variables.gms), default set in CAPRI's GUI configuration (not in the code supplied). CONSEQUENCE: the model's default (use_manure_market = False) is the faithful setup for validating against JRC121368; market-on scores against that study compared with a run that had no trade and are not evidence against the market. The market remains a valid option (CAPRI's newer manureTradeNew mode) without published results to validate against.

Switch CAPRIModel.use_manure_techs (default False, carried to projections). TEST six countries, N target only, 8 iterations: off -> pigs -21.9, dairy -4.4, N surplus -39.7%, reported/row 1.000; on -> shares LowEmHous 0.49, CovStorHigh 0.42, CovStorLow 0.19, AmmAppHE 0.42, AmmAppLE 0.61, ManAcid 0.43, AirPur 0.28; pigs -20.4, dairy -4.2, N surplus -66.7% (!), reported/row median 1.013. mitigation_in_supply.genetics_calibration: CAPRI calibrates genetics adoption (breeding.gms l. 350-460) with TWO calibration runs of the full model (ghgTechCali = ini and max, costParLin = 1e-10): marginal savings sav0 at the initial share m0 and sav1 at the maximum m1 (costsavings_ini/max GDX, v_miti marginals). Quadratic term gamma = [sav1 - sav0 + costParLin (relsubs1 - relsubs0)] / (m1 - m0) (ad-hoc fix against negative values), beta = sav0 - (1 - relsubs0) costParLin - gamma m0. mitigation_in_supply.fert_cost_basis: CAPRI's fertiliser-option costs are per TONNE of crop N need: GHG_Mit_Cost_ (supply_model.gms l. ~5062) multiplies the cropMiti options by -v_netPutQuant(NITF) x (1 + sum share x NMIN). market_newton_solver.note: MarketModule.market_solver = 'root' (default): SciPy optimize.root (Powell hybrid, finite-difference Jacobian) on the same equations as tatonnement - relative excess demand (demand - supply)/supply = 0 per commodity (39 world prices) - in log price ratios; accepted when max residual < 1e-6 and no price below the floor (half the base price), else tatonnement (old method, 1% tolerance) as fallback. CAPRI solves its market model as a system of equations with CONOPT. Full-EU run (baseline + 2030 Farm-to-Fork): Newton used in 9 of 9 market solves, residuals 1e-13 to 1e-16 (two baseline solves flag 'no progress' because they start at the solution, residual 2e-16), ~50 function evaluations, 3.5 s/solve (tatonnement 3.2); outer loop 7 iterations instead of 8; total 202 s vs ~250 s; all twenty indicators within 0.2 points; mean deviation from CAPRI 5.28 vs 5.24. 61/61 tests, anchors 8/8.

feed_in_supply.note: Project lead: do as CAPRI unless there are good reasons not to. CAPRI supply_model.gms: v_feedInpCoeff (kg feed per head) in REQSN_ (<= dry matter, fibre) and REQSE_ (= energy, protein; low-N feed, genetics, nitrate, linseed built in), FEDUSE_ (feed use = per-head feed x herd / 1000), SUPBAL_ (fodder), QUADRF_/QUADRF1_ (feed PMP = herd x sum feed (CNST + 0.5 SLOP feed)), GWPCH4ENT_ (CATTLE ENTERIC CH4 FROM THE FEED MIX: sum emission per kg feed x feed per head x herd - capri-mod uses a fixed factor per head), feed-share limits. Reformulation with total feed F = per-head x herd: all linear except the feed PMP, which becomes 0.5 SLOP F^2/x (perspective of a quadratic) - a second-order cone; each regional model becomes one convex conic program, solved exactly by Clarabel, with its multipliers replacing the re-detection of binding constraints. Replaces feed/ration.py and the ration loop. Fodder-at-shadow-price damping/bounds (not CAPRI) superseded. Plus a wider coupling review: joint vs separate modules, activity detail (CAPRI intensity variants and age classes vs 9 animals; ~50 vs 34 crops), commodities/processing (dairy, biofuels).

FIX: HERD_ALIASES moved to module level in capri_mod/data/loaders.py and used by the builder; fodder balance rebuilt (235 regions, 686 balances, base residual 9e-13 kt); usable fodder per ha rises (DEA1 grass 22.5 -> 28.0 t/ha, IE05 20.7 -> 29.1). build_young_animals.py has the same raw read (output unused). feed_in_supply.unbounded_regions: PL81/PL84/FI1D investigated. Negative feed objective coefficients (price + CNST) are normal - offset at base by the requirement duals, and every feed is held by its PMP curvature in the cone. The original quadratic part is positive definite in these regions (min eigenvalue 0.004-1.2; no zero-curvature variable), so the herd/crop/land part is bounded. Clarabel's DualInfeasible certificate for PL81 is ~0 in every component (objective slope -1.7): NUMERICAL rather than structural. Candidates: magnitudes in the national-fallback rations (e.g. heifers 20,450 kg grass per head, inflated per-head scale), equilibration limits, or near-redundant share rows. NEXT: re-solve with alternative scaling (per-row normalisation of requirement/share rows), check the share rows' consistency (sum of minimum shares), and test with herds fixed to isolate the feed block.

feed_in_supply.enteric_from_feed: CAPRI GWPCH4ENT_ (supply_model.gms l. 3051): cattle CH4ENT = sum_feed p_emisFeed(r,act,feed,'CH4ENT') x feed per head x herd x 0.001 x mitigation factors; non-cattle Tier 1 per head. p_emisFeed CH4ENT (envind/gases.gms l. 365-376, when CH4ENTfromFEED on) = Ym / 55.65 x GE (Mcal/kg DM) x 4.1868 x dry-matter content; Ym = EMISCALC(r,act,A,'YM') with EU value as fallback (source step still to trace); GE per feed group (envind/digestibility.gms l. 205-225) = average over component feedstuffs (ROWS) weighted by national feed use (FEDM + INTF) x dry matter; GE per feedstuff (l. ~134, NRC) = CP%/100 x 5.6 + FAT%/100 x 9.4 + (100 - CP - FAT - ASH)/100 x 4.2. Neither Ym nor GE is in the project yet (rations carry ENNE, CRPR, DRMA only; gd_full has no YM/GE). NEXT: check p_nutCont (fedcof) for CP/FAT/ASH per feedstuff, the feedstuff-to-feed-group map and national feed-use weights in the capreg dumps; trace Ym.
feed_in_supply.enteric_sources: All inputs of CAPRI's feed-based enteric CH4 are in its code: (1) NRC 2001 / INRA 2002 composition table TABLE p_digestPar(*,COLS,*,DIGSET) in envind/def_digestibility.gms (rows EU.DCOL.<feedstuff>; columns PAF DM CP NDICP ADICP EE NDF ADF LI ASH CAT; ~50 feedstuffs), copied to all regions and animals, grass built from pasture/silage/hay and legume variants by grazing share and N-fixation rate (default 0.05, max 0.75); FAT = EE - 1 (EE >= 1); GE (Mcal/kg DM) = CP/100 x 5.6 + FAT/100 x 9.4 + (100 - CP - FAT - ASH)/100 x 4.2. (2) Ym from TABLE EMISCALC0 in envind/create_rawdat_gascoeff_gdx.gms (IPCC 2006 Tables 10A.1-10A.2; EU000000: DCOW/DCOH/DCOL/SCOW/calves 0.065; regional values from inventories, EU fallback). (3) Feedstuff -> feed group FEED_TO_O (sets.gms l. 5622), weights = national FEDM + INTF x DM. p_emisFeed CH4ENT = Ym / 55.65 x GE x 4.1868 x DM content. NEXT: tools/build/build_enteric_feed_factors.py (parse both tables with the positional-table parser, map, weight from the capreg dumps), then cattle enteric CH4 from the regional feed totals F in the accounts; then market feed demand from F.
feed_in_supply.enteric_builder: tools/build/build_enteric_feed_factors.py -> capri_data/2017/environment/enteric_feed_factors.csv (1,215 rows: 27 countries x 5 cattle types x 9 feed groups; GE in Mcal/kg DM, Ym, grazing share). Parser rewritten (key = text before the first number; numbers to the header column with the nearest right edge): first version misread SWHE as DM 4.0 / CP 0.4 (table: 89.4 / 14.2) and truncated EMISCALC0 keys. NRC composition found for 38 feedstuffs; empty rows (POTA, OLIV, OOIL, OVEG, OFRU, TAGR, TABO, TWIN, SUGA, EGGS, PORK, BEEF...) are filled in CAPRI from 'similar products' (DEF_PRD) - here the group average of available members (REGISTERED). Grass: grazing share (RCEmissions) x pasture + rest 1/2 silage 1/2 hay, legume variants by n/0.75 with CAPRI's default n = 0.05 (REGISTERED). Ym 0.065 for all cattle (IPCC 2006, EU000000). Median GE: FCER 4.385, FGRA 4.184, FMAI 4.257, FPRO 4.634, FSTR 3.979, FOFA 4.115, FENE 3.961, FMIL 5.356, FOTH 5.935. Check: 0.065/55.65 x 4.2 x 4.1868 = 0.021 kg CH4/kg DM -> ~133 kg CH4 per dairy cow at 6,500 kg DM (IPCC EU ~117-128). NEXT: cattle enteric CH4 = sum feed F x Ym/55.65 x GE x 4.1868 x DM content (ration DRMA) in the accounts when feeding inside is on; then market feed demand from F; full-EU Farm-to-Fork.

feed_in_supply.full_eu_feed_based_ch4: Tests 61/61. Full-EU 2030 Farm-to-Fork with use_feed_in_supply ON and feed-based cattle enteric CH4: converged in 8, 788 s (default 7, ~240 s). Base EU enteric CH4 114,339 -> 169,606 kt CO2-eq (+48%; EU inventory ~6.5 Mt CH4 enteric ~160 Mt CO2-eq at GWP 25); change under Farm-to-Fork -7.4% in both (CAPRI -14.6%); dairy -5.2 vs -5.4, beef animals -6.4 vs -6.8 (CAPRI -10 / -18); all else within 0.8 point. Market feed demand from F still to connect.

feed_in_supply.runtime_profile: FR + DE (60 regions), baseline + 3 Farm-to-Fork iterations: OFF 72 s, built-in QP 14,128 calls x 0.4 ms = 5.8 s; ON 117 s, conic 3,459 calls x 14.1 ms = 48.9 s (+ built-in 10,495 x 0.1 ms). One region (FRH0), 20 solves: 17 ms per call = Clarabel 9.3 ms (~40 iterations at 1e-9, ~200 variables, 65 cones) + Python assembly ~8 ms. PLAN: build each region's static structure once and update only prices, changing coefficients (N row, fodder) and right-hand sides; tolerance 1e-8 if base reproduction holds; Clarabel in-place data updates.
feed_in_supply.fast_path: solve_with_feed_fast (feed_conic.py): feed block cached per region (rows, cones, scaling by BASE herds, compensation, fodder columns), sparse assembly, tolerance 1e-8. All 248 regions at base: median difference from the original path 0.009%, time per call 13.9 -> 11.0 ms only (Clarabel ~40 iterations dominates; median iterations 42.5 -> 40.5 at 1e-8). EIGHT regions differ although BOTH report Solved: ES70 12.5%, PL72 3.3%, PL81 3.5%, PL82 5.6%, PL84 3.8%, SI03 9.7%, BE22 100%, AT22 100% (AT22 'AlmostSolved' on the original path). Hypothesis: FLAT DIRECTIONS (non-unique optimum) - e.g. feeds with zero calibration curvature letting feed and herd trade off at no cost; the paths differ only in scaling and tolerance, which select different optimal points. NOT wired in. NEXT: check uniqueness in these regions (feeds with slope ~0, rank of the active constraints, the activity that differs), then decide the fast path; the run-time target needs fewer Clarabel iterations or fewer calls rather than faster assembly.
feed_in_supply.fast_path_fixed: CACHE BUG: the fast path keyed each region's feed block by id(rations); Python reuses a freed dict's address, so a later region could hit an earlier region's block (erratic 'divergences' up to 100% in BE22, AT22, ES70, SI03). Fixed: the block keeps a reference to its rations and each hit checks identity. After the fix, all 248 regions 'Solved' on the fast path; differences from the original path only in the four Polish fallback regions (PL72 3.3, PL81 3.5, PL82 5.6, PL84 3.8%, small BCOW/SHGP herds; national-scale land-market data); elsewhere median 0.0085%; base reproduction median 0.23%, 90th pct 0.52%. Genuinely flat: the FODDER MIX within animals - fodder calibration slopes ~1e-7..1e-8 (slope = price / (elasticity x base amount): cheap, large amounts), so fodders substitute almost freely (e.g. AT22 dairy roots 33 vs 80 t) while herds stay unique. Speed: 13.5 -> 10.9 ms per call (Clarabel ~40 iterations dominates). NEXT: Polish fallback land-market scaling at its source; decide default; run time via fewer solves (inner N-price loop).
feed_in_supply.fast_wired: Tests 61/61 after the land-market fix. Fast path wired into RegionalSupplyModel._feed_conic_solve (activities scaled by base levels, auxiliaries by the start point). The cache never hit at first: CAPRIModel._update_rations rebuilt the per-region rations dicts every iteration; now built once per ration model and reused (only prices change). FR+DE (60 regions), feeding inside ON: baseline 43 -> 15 s; Farm-to-Fork 3 iterations 111 -> 92 s; 11.6 ms per conic solve. Corrected count of solves per region over 3 outer iterations: median 52, 90th pct 107, max 128 (~17-40 per outer iteration) - the INNER N-price fixed point (fertiliser technologies, ammonia measures, rations respond to lambda outside the optimisation, _apply_balance_price) dominates run time, for the default model too. NEXT: reduce inner iterations (secant/Newton step on lambda instead of bracketing; or bring those responses into the regional problem, as CAPRI does with v_Miti).
feed_in_supply.techs_in_conic: SANDBOX RESET mid-turn (2026-10-08): repo restored from the 13:18 package, GAMS sources from uploads/gams.zip, Clarabel from the uploaded wheel; capreg dumps and land export not yet restored (only needed to rebuild data). Stage 1 of 'technologies as CAPRI v_Miti': solve_with_feed_fast(techs=..., n_row=...) adds M = share x herd per animal and ammonia technology: 0 <= M <= max x herd; stage sums <= herd; cost stock x [(k1 + beta) M + 0.5 k2 M^2/herd] (rotated cone), beta = -k1 - k2 s0 (ammo_tech.gms); N row -sub x ret x (M - s0 x herd). Not yet used by the model. BASE TEST (FRH0, DEA1; no N row): activities unchanged (<= 0.05%); shares: with k2 floor 1e-6 k1 zero shares drifted (flat at solver tolerance); with floor 0.01 k1 (K2_FLOOR, centred on s0) median |share - s0| 0.0014 / 0.0006 but max 0.17 and only 6 of 28 zero shares stay at zero - the tolerance is relative to the whole objective (dominated by PMP terms), so curvature small enough for CAPRI's corners cannot be resolved. DESIGN DECISION: technologies matter only through the N row -> (i) no N row: leave them out (shares = s0, as CAPRI starting from calibration); (ii) N row binding: include (benefit dominates); (iii) N row slack (dual ~0): report shares at s0 (CAPRI/CONOPT stays at the initial optimum). NEXT: implement (i)-(iii), wire into _feed_conic_solve, disable the external _apply_manure_techs when internal, results/reporting from M, then the inner N-price loop.

feed_in_supply.fert_techs_design: Fertiliser technologies: 9 options per MS (FERTTIME, GComTN, GComVN, NITR_INH, PRECFARM, VRT_H/L/M, VarRTech_X), NMIN 0.05-0.71, a 1.6-60.4 EUR/ha, b 8-302, s0 0, max 0.3-1.0. feed_in_supply.fert_inside: Fertiliser technologies inside, exact convex form (user decision: write the non-linearity in a form the solver handles exactly). feed_conic.solve_regional_conic: generic assembly of blocks (feed, ammonia technologies, fertiliser technologies); per fertilised crop m_c x (area_c + sum_t NMIN_t H_ct) >= n_c area_c^2 (rotated cone; CAPRI mineral N x (1 + E) = need, per crop - exact), H_ct adopted hectares (0 <= H <= max x area, sum <= area), cost a H + 0.5 b H^2/area (cone; s0 = 0); the crop's mineral part n_c = nmin x intensity x sqrt(yield / base yield) leaves its N-row coefficient and m_c enters with +1. Check: with feed only the new assembly reproduces the validated fast path bit for bit (6 regions incl. IE05, PL81). feed_in_supply.fert_active_set: FINDING (affects the DEFAULT model too - the external mechanism uses the same list): GComTN and GComVN are COMBINATIONS (CombinedEmissionMap in prep_gains_data_jul15.gms: GComTN = FertTime + NITR_INH, GComVN = VarRTech_X + NITR_INH); the block that builds them is commented out ($ontext...$offtext) in current CAPRI ('upper bound for combinations is always at 100% (may be questioned)'). Both contain inhibitors (max 0.3) but carry max 1.0 in our table, so with crop-specific adoption they took all fertilised hectares in FRH0. The endotech reference used by the Green Deal scenarios (refpol_endotech_all_sup.gms l. 218) activates ONLY ghgTechActiveFert = PRECFARM, VRT_SRUC, FERTTIME, NITR_INH (ghgMiti.gms l. 184 removes others). VRT_SRUC = SRUC variable-rate technology with NUTS2-level QEmitt, aggregated to NUTS0 (ghgMiti.gms l. 52-57); NOT in our table (which has the older GAINS VRT_L/M/H, VarRTech_X and the combinations). PLAN: (1) restrict fertiliser technologies to CAPRI's active set for Farm-to-Fork (setting, default = the endotech list) in _fert_techs; (2) VRT_SRUC data from the user's CAPRI installation (p_ghgMiti entries for VRT_SRUC: QEmitt, costParLin/Sqr, IniShare, MaxShare at NUTS2), or omit and register; (3) re-validate the default model (tests, anchors, full-EU Farm-to-Fork) and the inside path.
feed_in_supply.gcom_check: ENVIRONMENT MOVED (2026-10-08 ~18:00): repo restored from the 17:58 package (= 15:39 state), GAMS from uploads/gams.zip, Clarabel from the uploaded wheel; libraries now numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, pandas 3.0.5 - tests 61/61 (324 s). GComTN / GComVN in CAPRI (sets.gms 4056; prep_gains_data_jul15.gms 115-125, 470-505): 'Combination Timing and Nitrification Inhibitors' / 'Combination of Variable Rate Technology and Nitrification Inhibitors'; QEmitt = NOC x product of the components' reduction shares; costParLin = sum of the components' (21.2 = 4.0 + 17.2 net of pmpParLin); MaxShare = 1 by design ('may be questioned'). Options compete through TotMit_ (supply_model.gms: all options + NOC = 1), same as sum H <= area here. a, b are CAPRI's p_ghgMiti (costParLin + pmpParLin, costParSqr + pmpParSqr; pmpParSqr = costParLin for these options, NITR_INH costParLin/0.3) - not a model-made rule. So full adoption of the combinations in high-N-price regions (FRH0) follows from CAPRI's own parameters. JRC121368 Table 17 (EU, % of ELIGIBLE area): nitrification inhibitors 0 -> 18 (61% eligible), precision farming 0 -> 35 (60% eligible) = ~11% and ~21% of all area. Check by EU-wide adoption from the full run (tools/run/run_f2f_2030.py now saves area-weighted fertiliser and head-weighted ammonia shares; tools/check/compare_runs.py prints them grouped as Table 17). feed_in_supply.fert_capri_limits: CORRECTION: GComTN / GComVN are GAINS COMBINATIONS (sets.gms: timing + nitrification inhibitors; variable-rate technology + nitrification inhibitors), not green-cover options. CAPRI has no constraint linking combinations to components (prep_gains_data_jul15.gms block commented out; supply model has none); max share 1 as in our data. WHAT CAPRI DOES HAVE and the model lacked (default and inside paths alike), with restMitFert ON (endotech reference): (1) Tot_MitFert_ (supply_model.gms l. ~4136): 1 + sum_t v_Miti(t) NMIN_t <= max(v_cropNutNeedMultFact.l(r,NITF,T) + p_OverFertMarkUp, 1), p_OverFertMarkUp = 0.1 (envind/ghgMiti.gms l. 287) - technologies can only save over-fertilisation; (2) regional MaxShare (ghgMiti.gms l. 290-330): for options other than NITR_INH, where x + 0.1 > 1 and e(need) = e(noc)/(x + 0.1) > e(precfarm): maxshare = min(maxshare, (e(noc) - min(e(noc), e(tech) + e(need) - e(precfarm))) / (e(noc) - e(tech))); TotMitFertMin_ = per-option MaxShare (already applied). IMPLEMENTED: supply_module.overfert_factor / fert_efficiency_cap (OVERFERT_MARKUP 0.1; one warning per run while data missing); _fert_techs applies (2) (national QEmitt, CAPRI's NoSD branch); external rule applies (1) by bisection on the effective N price (= KKT with one multiplier on efficiency); conic model adds sum_ct NMIN_t H_ct <= cap x fertilised area. MECHANISM TEST (in-memory x = 1.1, cap 0.2, FRH0 + DEA1, Farm-to-Fork 3 iterations): E = 0.2000 on both paths; external vs inside shares nearly identical (GComTN 0.124/0.125, GComVN 0.146/0.142, NITR_INH 0.026/0.029); regional max shares FERTTIME/VRT 0, PRECFARM 0.46, GCom 0.52-0.54; N price DEA1 ~2 -> 37-42 EUR/kg. LIKELY KEY TO THE CATTLE GAP: unlimited fertiliser technologies let half the cattle regions comply almost for free. DATA PENDING: x = p_CropNutNeedMultFact(ru,NITF,T,2030) from results\fert\priFertDist_<MS>1730*.gdx (uploads/export_fert_out.csv is empty, 24 bytes); builder tools/build/build_overfert_factors.py -> capri_data/2017/environment/crop_nut_need_mult_fact_2030.csv. Product values: CAPRI final-product quantity (COMI, BEEF, PORK, POUM, EGGS, SGMT) x national UVAG x LEVL / model heads, by market (columns ACT.MARKET); a market price change moves an animal's revenue by quantity x price change, product by product.
pig_split_and_product_values.why_not_MREV: CAPRI's MREV differs by activity: for SOWS it is piglet sales (DE94: 24.0 x 25.43 = 610.9 = MREV), for raised calves CAMR/CAFR and replacement heifers HEIR it is young-animal sales (DEA2: CAMR MREV 623.7 = UVAG YBUL; HEIR 1071.4 = UVAG YCOW), for suckler cows a quarter of their beef value. Moving MREV with the meat price double-counted young animals (also priced by the young-animal markets) for sows, calves and heifers and under-moved suckler cows 2.9x.

pig_split_and_product_values.result: F2F 2030 gap 6.75 -> 7.02 (split alone) -> 6.91 (with product values); beef animals -14.5% (CAPRI -18), beef production -14.4% (-14); sows and fatteners fall together (-29%) because nitrogen prices in the pig regions exceed the fattener margin, so the piglet market does not relocate fattening

capri_baseline_surplus_regional.note: The tiered Farm-to-Fork N target starts from CAPRI's own baseline surplus per ha. The earlier file matched only CAPRI codes in the newest NUTS version and gave 82 regions their own surplus pattern scaled to CAPRI's national value - a proxy, although CAPRI's regional values were in capri_gnb_components_2030.csv under old NUTS codes (Italy, Belgium-Luxembourg, Sweden, Finland, Bulgaria, Romania, Poland, Hungary, Ireland). Rebuilt by tools/build/build_capri_baseline_surplus.py through shared/nuts_version_correspondence.json plus NUTS splits and merges (FI1D = FI13 + FI1A UAAR-weighted; ITH1/2 <- IT31; DED2/4/5 <- DED0; PL72/81/82/84/91/92; HU11/12 <- HU10; IE04/05/06 <- IR01/IR02). Valle d'Aosta 250 -> 48.5 kg N/ha (cut 70% -> 26%), Luxembourg 235 -> 157, Swedish regions ~100 -> 70-79, Piemonte 216 -> 97, Romania RO31 -89 -> 27; the nine capped regions are unchanged.

capri_region_groups.note: CAPRI regional tables were mapped to model regions with a first-candidate rule on the NUTS correspondence. Where CAPRI's region was later split, the whole parent went on one part: Finland's FI1B (Helsinki-Uusimaa) carried all of Etelae-Suomi's manure, revenue, costs and land on its own herd and area (990 kg N per dairy cow, 4.8 kg N per laying hen; arable land 709 kha on 121 kha of crops), FI1C took Laensi-Suomi's (FI190000 -> FI1C, a wrong correspondence entry), and renamed or split regions (Poland's PL72/81/82/84/91/92, Saxony, Bolzano/Trento, Budapest, Ireland, merged FI1D) took national averages. tools/lib/_model_regions.py now holds the NUTS splits and merges (SPLITS_MERGES, CORR_FIXES) and builds region groups (capri_groups): count-type tables (per-head output, revenue, costs, manure N, feed, premiums, young animals, rations) divide a group's CAPRI total by the group's model herd; ratio tables (shares, factors, per-ha terms) take the group's CAPRI region (region_to_capri; shared/region_capri_map.csv, also read at runtime). Rebuilt: livestock_*_coef, livestock_manure_n_coef, livestock_feed_coef, feed_ration_2017, young_animals_2017, fodder_balance_2017, nh3_factors_capri, ammonia_tech_model (dead rows for non-model codes dropped), manure_n2o_*, fert_side_effects, cover_crops, winter_cover_share, grass_intensity, dairy_intensity, histosol, plant_protection_cost, capri_baseline_surplus_2030; land_market_2017 re-split from its own entries (build_land_market.py --repair-splits; FI1B/FI1C from FI18, PL81/82/72/84 from their own CAPRI regions, AT12/AT13). Outliers beyond 3x the median per-head manure N: 79 -> 46 (the rest bulls and heifers, a herd-definition difference). Only the 19-24 affected regions changed in any file.

cattle_intensity_split.note: CAPRI fattens bulls and heifers in a low- and a high-intensity activity (BULL/BULH, HEIL/HEIH; equal numbers at base) that differ in fattening length (DE94 bulls 173 vs 270 days, heifers 78 vs 223), slaughter weight, daily feed and manure; each takes one young animal. The model's BULL and HFRS are census heads (stalls), so per stall-year flow items scale with 365/days. One column per animal moves stalls from high to low (bounds from the stall shares; HFRS includes the replacement heifers HEIR, which do not move), calibrated on the base duals like the dairy split; it enters the manure rows, the feed requirement rows, beef output, the young-animal balance and the young-animal price term. REGISTERED: regions without CAPRI's PMP terms take the country's median curvature x heads. Farm-to-Fork 2030: low-intensity bull stalls 33.6% -> 34.1%, heifers 7.2% -> 6.5%; EU aggregates within 0.2 points.

biofuel_feedstock_in_market.note: Crushing stage 4: CAPRI's biofuel block in the market (biofFeedCost_, biofFeedCostAgg_, Biof_, prodBiof_) at fixed biofuel output, as CAPRI runs scenarios without endogenous biofuel markets (arm/prep_market.gms p_endoBioMarket=0, arm/fix_biofuel_market_vars.gms). Superseded as the default by biofuel_markets_endogenous (Sprint 9c): star 3.0's GUI default is BIOF_M on, so the output is endogenous; the CES runs at that output in every CAPRI market region. Per member state from the 2030 reference; reproduces CAPRI's BiofFeedCost exactly. Replaces the post-solve BiofuelModule (hard-coded yields, feedstock splits and blending share). REGISTERED: DDGS and palm oil prices at the 2030 reference (no model market); glycerine fixed at 600 EUR/t as in CAPRI.

dairy_processing_block.note: CAPRI's dairy processing in the market (DairyNQ_, ProcMargM_, FatsProtBal_) per member state with p_hessNQDairy; raw milk priced by its fat and protein; nine products, four traded (BUTR, SKIM, CHES, WHEY), five cleared in the EU (FRMI, CREM, COCM, WMIO, CASE). Sheep and goat milk is raw milk. REGISTERED: EU-common price ratios of fat, protein and raw milk; the five EU-cleared products keep extra-EU trade, feed and industrial use at the 2030 reference.

dairy_world_markets_fao_agg.note: World base balances of butter, skimmed milk powder, cheese and whey from CAPRI's FAO_agg. Before: BUTT/SMIP/WHEP codes never matched the market's BUTR/SKIM/WHEY (invented shares of hard-coded world totals) and the primary cheese item was not cheese (USA 28 kt vs 5,889).

eu_price_single_premium.note: MarketModule.solve reported the EU price as wedge x premium x premium (the premium loop wrote wedge x premium into the domestic prices and the report multiplied again). Supply always saw world x premium once; reported EU price changes of all premium commodities were inflated (Farm-to-Fork cereals +10.4% reported vs +5.7% paid).

cattle_genomics_in_supply.note: breeding.gms genet_yld (dairy cows, ghgTechMYld: a CAPRI scenario setting, default 0 as star 3.0's refpol_endotech_all_sup, 0.2 in the JRC121368-era ecampa references; applied to baseline and scenario alike, capri_mod/policy/endotech.py) and genet_eff (non-dairy ruminants except HEIR and milk sheep, ghgTechFEff 0.1) as columns of the regional supply models: effects on manure rows and feed requirements, milk revenue, CAPRI's calibration (linear term from base duals + relSubs0 x cost, gamma = max(0.2c, c(relSubs1-relSubs0))). REGISTERED: the ini/max marginal-value drop CAPRI subtracts from gamma is left to the supply model's own curvature.

world_market_baseline_fao_agg.note: Every region's base balance from CAPRI's FAO_agg BAS for 32 market commodities. Before: a FAO extract whose 'SUGR' was sugar cane (world sugar 1,768 Mt vs CAPRI 168), invented world totals split by fixed regional shares (pork 171 Mt vs 120, eggs 126 vs 84, maize 1,591 vs 1,136, wine 70 vs 27) and EU self-sufficiency from a different extract. DWHE, PARI, OOIL, OLIV have no CAPRI world balance under a matching product and keep the old base (REGISTERED).
